If you spend enough time reading the news these days, it's easy to conclude that America is coming apart.
Trust in government is near [historic lows](https://substack.com/redirect/0358649d-904d-4471-8762-aa1e353a7255?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [trust in the media](https://substack.com/redirect/d542d8f9-fd3e-40e4-b6b1-990ee2981d0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) isn't much better. Religious participation has [declined](https://substack.com/redirect/03582a8e-08ee-4361-91dd-7863857820fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and Americans feel increasingly [disconnected](https://substack.com/redirect/b5813683-3725-4fb0-a75a-79181b20631d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from their communities.
But a few weeks ago, standing on stage at Florida Atlantic University (FAU), I found a reason to feel hopeful about the future.
I was there to deliver the keynote address to the 19 Army ROTC cadets earning the rank of second lieutenant. The average GPA of this cohort was 3.56.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dab06df4-32f6-4f9e-805a-b02a4d1789ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The ceremony itself was historic for FAU as it was the first commissioning class for the newly established Talon Battalion, led by Lieutenant Colonel Keith Weaver, a combat veteran and fellow 82nd Airborne paratrooper who has helped build one of the fastest growing ROTC programs.
Watching them take their sacred oath to support and defend the Constitution, I was reminded that for all the reasons people have lost faith in America, there are still young men and women willing to commit themselves to something bigger than themselves.
Roughly [5,000](https://substack.com/redirect/84bfef88-1a29-4a38-8587-46b9dbd0ad5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) young men and women have earned their commissions as Army officers every year through ROTC programs across the country. They are the ones who wake up at 5:30 am to do physical training (PT), take leadership classes, spend two weekends at field training exercises each semester, conduct summer training in the scorching heat, and manage a full load of classes in order to compete and earn their second lieutenant rank.
One of these new FAU lieutenants was Paul McCullough IV. His father and I were cadets together at Kings College in Wilkes-Barre thirty years ago. I looked at this kid taking the same oath his father took, and I had to remind myself to keep it together since I've known him since he was a toddler.
When I joined the ROTC program in 1993, there were only three cadets. By the time we graduated, there were 30. Leadership has a way of multiplying itself (thanks to the mentorship of two U.S. Army Armor Captains Bob Thomas and Joe O'Donnell leading from the front). In May 1996, four of us were commissioned as second lieutenants.
The commencement speaker that day at King's College was Republican Governor Tom Ridge.
Ridge was a decorated Vietnam combat veteran, Harvard grad, and former U.S. Congressman from Erie, Pennsylvania who would later become the nation's first Secretary of Homeland Security after the attacks of 9/11. But on that afternoon, he wasn't a national figure to me. He was simply there to help commission and congratulate a handful of young Army officers.
Ridge was a decorated Vietnam combat veteran, Harvard grad, and former U.S. Congressman from Erie, Pennsylvania who would later become the nation's first Secretary of Homeland Security after the attacks of 9/11. But on that afternoon, he wasn't a national figure to me. He was simply there to help commission and congratulate a handful of young Army officers.
I'll always remember how he stood up when our names were called to shake each of our hands, looking us in the eyes and saying "Congratulations Lieutenant, make us proud" when he just as easily could've stayed seated.
I made sure to follow in his footsteps and shake the hand of every single one of those 19 graduates at FAU. It was a hopefully moment that felt like passing the torch to the next generation.
## **Lessons from Commencements**
One of the greatest honors of my career has been delivering commencement addresses. Whether at the University of Pennsylvania [Fels School,](https://substack.com/redirect/9a9dec0e-03ef-4e5b-8eba-92db640e4104?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) my alma maters of [King's College](https://substack.com/redirect/6e08cb8d-c086-479f-8cf9-98d48a3599ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Widener University](https://substack.com/redirect/5d7cda82-521c-4e0a-9914-f701e5de5fc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), I always leave inspired and learn something from the graduating class.
Country star [Eric Church](https://substack.com/redirect/c44a69fd-49bb-4eac-99f3-3f2e312c3616?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) gave the commencement address at UNC this year, using his guitar and his "six strings of life" as a metaphor for success.
I also learned from Roger Federer, who spoke at Dartmouth in 2024 about mental toughness and shared a surprising stat: he won nearly 80 percent of his matches across his career, but only 54 percent of the points he played. That's a useful reminder for anyone beginning a new chapter in life. You will make mistakes. You will have setbacks. Some opportunities won't work out. Some plans will fail.
The goal isn't to avoid failure. The goal is to learn from it, reset, and keep moving forward.
Don't let one bad point convince you you've lost the match. Get up, dust yourself off, and keep getting after it.
As Americans, especially as we approach our 250th birthday, we can learn a lot from this young generation. Don't let those who discount or disparage young people shape your perspective. Instead of dictating to the next generation, empower them by investing your time and wisdom so they can flourish and lead.
You might be surprised by what you find if you're willing to look a little harder. They are light years away from my generation when it comes to digital fluency, social justice, adaptability and their entrepreneurial spirit. We just need to give them a chance, like Tom Ridge said to us thirty years ago, "Congratulations, now go make us proud!"

How a group of newly commissioned Army officers reenergized me about the future of America. | | | Jun 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | If you spend enough time reading the news these days, it's easy to conclude that America is coming apart. Trust in government is near and isn't much better. Religious participation has , and Americans feel increasingly from their communities. But a few weeks ago, standing on stage at Florida Atlantic University (FAU), I found a reason to feel hopeful about the future. I was there to deliver the keynote address to the 19 Army ROTC cadets earning the rank of second lieutenant. The average GPA of this cohort was 3.56. | | ---|---|--- The ceremony itself was historic for FAU as it was the first commissioning class for the newly established Talon Battalion, led by Lieutenant Colonel Keith Weaver, a combat veteran and fellow 82nd Airborne paratrooper who has helped build one of the fastest growing ROTC programs. Watching them take their sacred oath to support and defend the Constitution, I was reminded that for all the reasons people have lost faith in America, there are still young men and women willing to commit themselves to something bigger than themselves. Roughly young men and women have earned their commissions as Army officers every year through ROTC programs across the country. They are the ones who wake up at 5:30 am to do physical training (PT), take leadership classes, spend two weekends at field training exercises each semester, conduct summer training in the scorching heat, and manage a full load of classes in order to compete and earn their second lieutenant rank. One of these new FAU lieutenants was Paul McCullough IV. His father and I were cadets together at Kings College in Wilkes-Barre thirty years ago. I looked at this kid taking the same oath his father took, and I had to remind myself to keep it together since I've known him since he was a toddler. When I joined the ROTC program in 1993, there were only three cadets. By the time we graduated, there were 30. Leadership has a way of multiplying itself (thanks to the mentorship of two U.S. Army Armor Captains Bob Thomas and Joe O'Donnell leading from the front). In May 1996, four of us were commissioned as second lieutenants. The commencement speaker that day at King's College was Republican Governor Tom Ridge. Ridge was a decorated Vietnam combat veteran, Harvard grad, and former U.S. Congressman from Erie, Pennsylvania who would later become the nation's first Secretary of Homeland Security after the attacks of 9/11. But on that afternoon, he wasn't a national figure to me. He was simply there to help commission and congratulate a handful of young Army officers. Ridge was a decorated Vietnam combat veteran, Harvard grad, and former U.S. Congressman from Erie, Pennsylvania who would later become the nation's first Secretary of Homeland Security after the attacks of 9/11. But on that afternoon, he wasn't a national figure to me. He was simply there to help commission and congratulate a handful of young Army officers. I'll always remember how he stood up when our names were called to shake each of our hands, looking us in the eyes and saying "Congratulations Lieutenant, make us proud" when he just as easily could've stayed seated. I made sure to follow in his footsteps and shake the hand of every single one of those 19 graduates at FAU. It was a hopefully moment that felt like passing the torch to the next generation. Lessons from Commencements** One of the greatest honors of my career has been delivering commencement addresses. Whether at the University of Pennsylvania my alma maters of and , I always leave inspired and learn something from the graduating class. Country star gave the commencement address at UNC this year, using his guitar and his "six strings of life" as a metaphor for success. I also learned from Roger Federer, who spoke at Dartmouth in 2024 about mental toughness and shared a surprising stat: he won nearly 80 percent of his matches across his career, but only 54 percent of the points he played. That's a useful reminder for anyone beginning a new chapter in life. You will make mistakes. You will have setbacks. Some opportunities won't work out. Some plans will fail. The goal isn't to avoid failure. The goal is to learn from it, reset, and keep moving forward. Don't let one bad point convince you you've lost the match. Get up, dust yourself off, and keep getting after it. As Americans, especially as we approach our 250th birthday, we can learn a lot from this young generation. Don't let those who discount or disparage young people shape your perspective. Instead of dictating to the next generation, empower them by investing your time and wisdom so they can flourish and lead. You might be surprised by what you find if you're willing to look a little harder. They are light years away from my generation when it comes to digital fluency, social justice, adaptability and their entrepreneurial spirit. We just need to give them a chance, like Tom Ridge said to us thirty years ago, "Congratulations, now go make us proud!" The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. subject: This endorsement draws a stark contrast in this race
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
Our opponents are funded by corporate PACs. We're backed by the people who build things, who care for people, who keep this state running.
# [ ](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1218?t=1&akid=2316%2E251025%2E6YjGQm)
Peter, I have exciting news to share:
**The UAW — one of the largest and most powerful unions in the United States — just endorsed our campaign.**
[](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260605-1-ak.RYdP8z&amount=10&refcode=em20260605-2315&t=3&akid=2316%2E251025%2E6YjGQm)
UAW members have spent over 80 years fighting for the issues many corporate PAC-funded politicians are paid to ignore: fair wages, safe workplaces, and the right to organize.
My parents moved to Michigan to work in the thriving auto industry. Growing up, I saw what it meant to have a union at your back — the security of knowing your employer couldn't take advantage of you.
**Earning the UAW's endorsement is a real full-circle moment for my family and me.**
Peter, Michiganders deserve a senator who answers to them — not to the corporations and billionaires who have spent decades calling the shots.
This endorsement draws a stark contrast in this race: **our opponents are funded by corporate PACs. We're backed by the people who build things, who care for people, who keep this state running.**
[**That contrast is our winning message — and we need resources to get it in front of every undecided voter in Michigan before August 4th. Will you chip in today to fuel our work?**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260605-1-ak.RYdP8z&amount=10&refcode=em20260605-2315&t=4&akid=2316%2E251025%2E6YjGQm)

In solidarity,
Abdul

subject: The Only Weekend List That Matters: Elect Melat Kiros
body:
9 things to do with Team Kiros
| |
---
| Hi Peter, The weekend is upon us, and boy do we have something better than brunch plans. Actually, there is so much going on over the next three days, you can keep your brunch plans and still find plenty of ways to get in the game.
## 9 Things You Can Do This Weekend to Elect Melat Kiros
Friday **1\. Melat at June First Friday** The First Friday Art Walks are the signature event of Denver's Art District on Santa Fe. We'll have a table at El Museo, 861 Santa Fe Dr. [**Sign up here.**](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=101e6df9a6ce40a63d03b69250044664efa0706f&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Ftabling) Fri 5:30-9:30 **2\. Get your "Melat Kiros for Congress" yard sign** Show your support for Melat Kiros. Fill out this form and we will deliver a yard sign directly to your home. **[Request yours now.](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=035117f81ab2b98df513134dbb49470050392725&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Fyardsign)** Saturday **3\. Colorado DemFest** Melat will speak on the CD1 Forum hosted by Colorado DemFest, at the Denver Center for the Performing Arts. [**Sign up here.**](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=101e6df9a6ce40a63d03b69250044664efa0706f&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Ftabling) Sat 8am-3pm **4\. Saturday Canvass for Melat Kiros** Join us for a canvass in your area to chat with your neighbors about Melat's people-powered vision for our country. Whether you're a seasoned canvasser or have never knocked a door in your life, you are welcome and encouraged to attend. All canvasses will begin with a training, and you can always choose to go with a buddy. **[Sign up in your area.](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=6b49fd8a3dca767a4907dd8b354a2b9ff355e157&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Fcanvass)** Sat 12-3pm and 2:30-6:30pm **5\. Saturday Phonebank for Melat Kiros** Hop on the phones with us to call voters and tell them about the movement to get Melat Kiros elected to Congress. **[Sign up.](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=25f0ab90851ec98f1af040c669be796a9071ff65&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Fphonebank) **Sat 3-5pm **6\. Help us canvass in your apartment building.** So far, our volunteers have knocked thousands of doors across the city—now we're ready to take it to the next level by reaching our neighbors in apartment buildings. We need your help to make it happen. **[Sign up to volunteer.](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=a6bc9374ad30058176224954105f093bc366770d&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Fapartments)** Sunday **7\. South Pearl Farmers Market** Team Kiros will be talking to voters during the regular Sunday South Pearl Street Farmers Market. Second Star to the Right Bookstore. [**Sign up here.**](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=101e6df9a6ce40a63d03b69250044664efa0706f&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Ftabling) Sun 10am-1pm **8\. Sunday Canvass for Melat Kiros** Join us for a canvass in your area to chat with your neighbors about Melat's people-powered vision for our country. Whether you're a seasoned canvasser or have never knocked a door in your life, you are welcome and encouraged to attend. All canvasses will begin with a training, and you can always choose to go with a buddy. **[Sign up in your area.](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=6b49fd8a3dca767a4907dd8b354a2b9ff355e157&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Fcanvass) **Sun 11:30am-3:30 and 2-6pm **9\. City Park Jazz** This weekend is the first [Jazz in the Park](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=2a9d330862ca81aa844e8a863cac438e2ed0284d&url=https%3A%2F%2Fcityparkjazz.org%2F) of the summer! Join Team Kiros for smooth tunes and conversations with Denver voters. 1600 City Park Esplanade. [**Sign up here.**](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/jRGZVjEOQObIpH53359QYacdrKkWSdju/click?signature=101e6df9a6ce40a63d03b69250044664efa0706f&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwin.kirosforco.com%2Ftabling) Sun 6-8pm.
* * *
Phew! Beyond this, there are countless farmer's markets, fairs, Pride events, and who-knows-whats that you all are bringing our campaign into. Your energy and creativity are incredible — and the backbone of this campaign.. We have**25 days until the primary on June 30th. We need to reach 100,000 voters, and we need all hands on deck.** We'll be in touch again soon, with even more opportunities for you to find a place to contribute. We'll see you out there,**** Team Kiros

****

I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. What's different now is the pace. Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: ✅ Arkansas ✅ Florida ✅ Idaho ✅ Indiana ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Oklahoma ✅ South Carolina ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action. That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly. It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up. Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through. And right now, that's where we're stretched. We're not lacking interest or momentum. We're working to keep up with both. So here 's how you can help... Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it. An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: ✅ Constitutions. ✅ Chapter guides. ✅ Flags. ✅ Materials to organize and lead. It turns a student who wants to speak up... into one who actually does. And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here." Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines. That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward. That's how this movement actually scales. Because the reality is, the demand is here now. The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it. And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward. One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you. If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now. Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school. This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it. And we don't take that lightly. I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. Peter, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture. But moments like this don't sustain themselves. If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple. We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day. If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

body:
Make your first gift today and receive a FREE “God's Children Are Not For Sale” t-shirt as our thank-you.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e7287627/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvUUJLVjJFVnRZOA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA2MDU/LbmNsUEVYSURYUA/qP2hpZHM9bmNLS2tTYmo4QzhZNU1scw/gaiL3ug/s3uc586f53e)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| |
---
| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, I want to start with two simple words. **Thank you.** Thank you for caring about children you may never meet. Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold. Because that is exactly what is happening. **Every day.**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**God's children are not for sale.** And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth. When you make your first gift to the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** today, we'll send you a FREE white **"God's Children Are Not For Sale"** t-shirt as our thank-you.
---
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | | This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store. You can't buy it online. It was created exclusively for supporters of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say: **"No more."** Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters. **A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity.** And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. **Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself.** A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. **Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verástegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back. Jesus said, _"Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."_ (Matthew 19:14) **Every child is precious in God's eyes.** **Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth.** And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
When you make your first gift today, you help:
---
* **Prevent exploitation** by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children.

* **Support intervention efforts** by equipping trusted partners working to help rescue children trapped in exploitation.

* **Educate parents and communities** about the warning signs traffickers use to target children.

* **Raise awareness** so more people understand the reality of this crisis.

* **Advocate for stronger protections** for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers.

---
This is how change happens. **One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet.** **Today, that person can be you.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Will you make your first gift now? **[Please make your most generous gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can today to help protect vulnerable children from exploitation and trafficking.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Choose your shirt size and select a color. **And know that your generosity will help protect vulnerable children and bring hope to those who need it most.** Thank you for caring and for standing with vulnerable children. **Thank you for choosing action over silence**. With gratitude and prayer,
---
Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**P.S.** Your FREE "**God's Children Are Not For Sale** " t-shirt is available only for a limited time and only while supplies last. Please make your first gift today, choose your size, and join a growing movement committed to protecting vulnerable children. Every child matters. Every child deserves freedom.
---
[ Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074
---

108 S Washington St. Suite 200
Alexandria, VA 22314

Just days before his 19th birthday, my son Justin was out in the fields with us, doing what this family has done for over three generations—farming the Louisiana delta. A breakdown in our combine left corn spilled across the ground, and as we worked to recover it, Justin got too close. In an instant, his pant leg was caught, and the thresher pulled him in.
I can still hear his voice: “Dad, get me out.”
And there was nothing I could do.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Multiple miracles occurred that day: When it initially happened he wasn’t in pain because his nerves were pinched so tightly in the machine. Nor was he bleeding because he was caught so tight in there.
It took the jaws of life to tear apart that machine and when the metal finally gave way he let out a scream that I will never forget for the rest of my life.
The paramedics quickly sprang into action and he was airlifted to Jackson, Mississippi, where Doctors fought to save his leg, but the injury and infection from all the dirt and debris were too severe. Justin lost his leg from below the knee.
That day could have broken us. Instead, it showed me what makes Louisiana strong.
Neighbors, first responders from two parishes (what we call counties in Louisiana), and a doctor who wasn’t even on duty, Dr. Ron Gregg, a farmer himself and longtime family friend — showed up because that’s what rural communities do. They take care of each other. They don’t ask if it’s their job or jurisdiction. They just show up.
Today, Justin is 35. He runs our farm. He’s built a life, with a fiancée and a family of his own. He still hunts, fishes, and works the land — just with a prosthetic leg and the same determination that carried him through that day.
But the truth is, the kind of community that saved Justin is disappearing. Rural hospitals are closing. Doctors like Dr. Gregg—who live in our communities, who know our families—are harder to find. Too many of our kids feel like they have to leave home to build a future.
And my family, who first worked this Louisiana delta soil as slaves and sharecroppers, and now as farmers who own this land, have put too much blood into this soil for us to leave and go somewhere else.
I have to take a stand and fight for our way of life and it’s why I am proud to be the Democrat running for Senate in Louisiana.
If you believe in that fight, I’m asking you to stand with me today. A Democratic win here is the first step in taking our state back from the far-right whose policies of atomization and vicious corporatism are tearing our communities apart.
And mark my words, a win is possible, Democrats just won a deep red special election here by a landslide. The blue wave will wash over Louisiana and we will flip this seat but only if we fight for it. Will you please make a contribution of $50, $20, or even just $10 to help us in our fight to restore the Louisiana that we love so dearly. This Pride, your support powers the work that keeps LGBTQ+ immigrants safe, seen, and defended. A gift today says clearly: in our community, no one stands alone. | | | Peter, Happy Pride Month! This is a season of joy, celebration, and showing up loudly exactly as we are. _Pride was built by people who refused to be erased_ — a spirit that continues today through the immigrant youth and LGBTQ+ neighbors who power our movement. ✊🏽 🌈 **[This Pride, help us ensure every LGBTQ+ immigrant can live freely and safely. Please give $5 today to power our relentless work to protect our community.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeGy6-t39KkoipeLUgUbkqJt5ot29zSgOh_0oiUNbESFMJh-F6Ca6tsd45zdt1Nb5ZgB1pZ_mTqovDDurV0u1ZUgC3YV-xwC67Mvti96p0vSZ93prdS-RqU_eS53rWmgP7vhlCaplvruz_sFNjY3Lz4sH_BMTBbuS0atSKj58iSu4OhVEv0TNDlYztVbUpNlXlUhLLe_WKBN8CqUcOwV9IWOIXWm0wc1AMO-B4kEzbuMdDgewzKEe-virh1e-1bV38eB7c4d1_ATqY5JQUtXUc8vRCrW6vxe4jZbFUyvl5gga1kRUHcBREJU1PcdLH_zLAt1sproABouHYDob6rZ29pLSwoFlwd5Xg6kj9awZyCedKJYLxoQGw4ZK8hKzbwF0fUKIyt4o2mmZFDVWw8v0AEw/4r8/7cFBUDrpStil-97UTS0WWQ/h0/h001.Y6jrg8Agm5dbOswVIhpJNjg3adS5ejwgtAHEb7_MLAs)** We celebrate the powerful legacy of queer and trans immigrant youth at the heart of our movement. And we continue to organize because when LGBTQ+ immigrants in our community are detained, they face unique and severe dangers that we cannot ignore. Under this administration, the Department of Homeland Security has removed all mention of trans people from its detention practices, meaning trans women are often detained in wards or sections of detention camps with men, leaving them vulnerable to abuse.1 Trans and queer detainees are approximately **fifteen times more likely** to be sexually assaulted than others in detention, and many are denied essential hormone treatments or life-saving medical care.2 [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeGy6-t39KkoipeLUgUbkqJt5ot29zSgOh_0oiUNbESFMJh-F6Ca6tsd45zdt1Nb5ZzedLcisNpDwX41zDjFTRr4ykAjcyVadcd8zaqCqhTteddObGhfpIvJw8jJ6zWFteMMnw5yextGsfmIjvQGgdheO5h5EOmShX99pa1Xfpu2UJhjTpxdkXqXBZCfGKavnHrx__sNAF_I4lQ1-JsSE5s8YrUfb66gQrTqbTUbex-yxfbKO8IQH7a1uOyVdG1gMWen_tJ4vGZ1uEy5UFiG-Msl4pUd3pXjlnFK7_JOHPyb2VjrywAQSOyTdLXBt1t7dNYjB_68R20le4Ucp42cSRsO3vSC9xOfByrMZ9dpzQfmJjEIt_f8GpECatHldoOXzf/4r8/7cFBUDrpStil-97UTS0WWQ/h1/h001.OWHbppAUJyXPXUPaG8STUBAF3LVkP-k0vNB2JezlY0Q)
Others are placed in solitary confinement under the guise of "protective custody," despite the documented risk of irreversible psychological harm. And, for those seeking safety, the path is narrow: being LGBTQ+ is criminalized in over 77 countries, yet asylum remains profoundly difficult to secure. _These aren't just statistics; they are the realities of people we love._ And when those in our communities are hurting or targeted because of who they are, we have a responsibility to show up, organize, and take care of each other. **[This Pride, help us keep that commitment. clean_body: This Pride, your support powers the work that keeps LGBTQ+ immigrants safe, seen, and defended. A gift today says clearly: in our community, no one stands alone. | | | Peter, Happy Pride Month! This is a season of joy, celebration, and showing up loudly exactly as we are. Pride was built by people who refused to be erased — a spirit that continues today through the immigrant youth and LGBTQ+ neighbors who power our movement. ✊🏽 🌈 We celebrate the powerful legacy of queer and trans immigrant youth at the heart of our movement. And we continue to organize because when LGBTQ+ immigrants in our community are detained, they face unique and severe dangers that we cannot ignore. Under this administration, the Department of Homeland Security has removed all mention of trans people from its detention practices, meaning trans women are often detained in wards or sections of detention camps with men, leaving them vulnerable to abuse.1 Trans and queer detainees are approximately fifteen times more likely to be sexually assaulted than others in detention, and many are denied essential hormone treatments or life-saving medical care.2 Others are placed in solitary confinement under the guise of "protective custody," despite the documented risk of irreversible psychological harm. And, for those seeking safety, the path is narrow: being LGBTQ+ is criminalized in over 77 countries, yet asylum remains profoundly difficult to secure. These aren't just statistics; they are the realities of people we love. And when those in our communities are hurting or targeted because of who they are, we have a responsibility to show up, organize, and take care of each other. subject: Ignorant bulls--
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132775389/625643444/526203646?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGRlZGI5Mi0wMDYxLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ZK3_wlftDGo13HxAecLOyG5hbj7Pz_3b1FUeJOxZfoM=)
Peter, Pride Month can draw out the worst of them, but this triggered me in a whole extra way. A sitting member of Congress publicly declared that homosexuality has "no place in America" and then, when the backlash came, deleted it like the coward he is. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132775390/625643445/526203646?refcode=em-6.5.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGRlZGI5Mi0wMDYxLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ZK3_wlftDGo13HxAecLOyG5hbj7Pz_3b1FUeJOxZfoM=) I publicly called him out then, and let me say this here in the clearest terms: **What Rep. Andy Ogles said is ignorant, hateful, and pathetic, and it says far more about him and his failings as a person than it does about any LGBTQ+ person in this country.** As the first openly LGBTQ+ person elected to represent Illinois in Congress, I am not intimidated by comments like these. I've heard versions of them my entire life. I heard them growing up. I heard them when I lost a job because I was gay. And now I hear them from people serving in the same institution that Abraham Lincoln, the great uniter, once served in. **I know which side of history I want to be on.** I want to be on the side that expands freedom, not restricts it. I want to be on the side that welcomes people into our democracy, not tells them they don't belong. Jun 5 | | | | | | | | | Scott DesJarlais, the guy I am running against in TN-04, took two oaths. The first was the Hippocratic oath, the doctor's promise to do no harm. The second was the congressional oath, the legislator's promise to serve the people of this district with honesty, integrity, and conviction. He broke both. Publicly. Repeatedly, and without real world consequence... until now. As a doctor, public records show he pressured a mistress (who was also his patient, to get an abortion.) A direct, documented violation of the ethical boundary between physician and patient. Meanwhile, he spent 14 years voting to strip healthcare access from the very people who trusted him with their votes, calling the repeal of the Affordable Care Act his "number one priority." After years of trying to tear down our healthcare system, has Scott DesJarlais offered a serious plan to make it better? No. He collects a government paycheck, posts birthday memes on social media, and calls it leadership. Tennessee deserves better. | | ---|---|--- Tennessee is only as strong as its most vulnerable neighbor, only as prosperous as its struggling families, and only as successful as the children we leave behind. That's why it's time to send career politicians like Scott DesJarlais into retirement. Desjarlais wore a pro-life rating like a badge of honor while operating by a completely different set of rules behind closed doors. He accepted the endorsements, gave the speeches, and cashed the checks... all while building a record that is the single greatest argument against ever giving him another term. This isn't personal. It's a pattern. A man who has spent his entire career saying one thing and doing another deserves exactly one thing in return. A pink slip from the people he was elected to serve. Let's send someone to Washington who actually means what they say. Hey folks,
**Joe Walsh** and I sat down for a conversation that starts with a Senate race in Maine and quickly turns into something much bigger: accountability, redemption, power, and where we draw the line when politics asks us to look the other way.
We talked about what happens when winning becomes the only thing that matters. We talked about whether people can change. And we talked about why some standards can't be negotiable--even when the stakes feel enormous.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:13**] Joe jumps in with a surprising take on Tucker Carlson's future, while we kick off a conversation about the political stories dominating the week.
* [**00:07:13**] Joe lays out why he believes accountability starts with owning your mistakes--and why that matters for anyone seeking public office.
* [**00:11:26**] We discuss listening to the people most affected by political decisions, including women and Jewish voters wrestling with difficult choices.
* [**00:18:12**] The conversation shifts to Hunter Biden, redemption arcs, public scrutiny, and what earning trust actually looks like.
* [**00:33:45**] We close with a broader discussion about moral red lines, violence against women, and why abandoning core values comes with a cost.

At its core, this episode is about character. It's about whether redemption is possible, what accountability requires, and how we navigate political moments when every choice feels imperfect. body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=7015%2E582294%2E-kLlLi ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=7015%2E582294%2E-kLlLi ]Chris Pappas for Senate

I’m sorry about Karoline
Leavitt.

Before she was hand-picked as Donald Trump’s White House Press Secretary,
Karoline ran against me for Congress here in New Hampshire. She lost — by
nearly 10 points.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260605_2.KWyWru&refcode=em20260605-7015&amount=5&t=1003&akid=7015%2E582294%2E-kLlLi ][IMG]

But that campaign gave her exactly what she needed: a test run for the
MAGA talking points she now repeats from behind the White House podium.
She’s been practicing the spin for years — and while New Hampshire wasn’t
buying it, Trump was.

Let me be clear: I don’t regret a thing about standing up to Karoline and
her MAGA agenda — not then and not now.

This race is going to be tough. National Republicans and John Sununu are
doing everything they can to flip this seat. They’re recycling the same
extremist ideas, running the same playbook and relying on people like
Karoline Leavitt to carry their message.

We beat her once and with your help, we’ll do it again.

Thanks for being in this fight with me.

Chris Pappas

name: MassDems featuring Representative John Moran
subject: Celebrating Pride Month
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Fellow Democrats,
Each year, my husband and I eagerly await Pride Month. As a longtime resident of Boston’s South End, I have fond memories of celebrating with friends, dancing badly to Madonna, and, most importantly, finding the freedom to be myself alongside my LGBTQ+ family.
This year, Pride is bittersweet as we mourn the loss of Congressman Barney Frank, a trailblazer whose courage changed countless lives, including mine. I was in college when he became the first sitting member of Congress to come out.
Recently, constituent and Democratic activist Richard Shibley gave me a copy of Improper Bostonians signed by Barney shortly before his passing. I will always treasure it and remain committed to advancing the cause of equality.
Much has been written about Barney’s call for Democrats to be strategic in defending our values. But strategy should never mean silence when our rights are under attack. Earlier this week, after a Massachusetts MAGA Republican shared a graphic portraying Pride as evil and suggesting it be replaced with “American Pride Month,” I responded with a video challenging the false choice between loving your country and embracing your LGBTQ+ identity. Barney, I hope I got that right.
At the recent MassDems Convention in Worcester, I joined members of the LGBTQ+ Legislative Caucus for a conversation with community members, including several transgender individuals who relocated to Massachusetts from the South. They spoke candidly about the challenges of affording housing and building new lives here. Their stories reinforced the importance of continuing our work to make Massachusetts more affordable and welcoming for everyone.
Pride is about celebration, but it is also about standing up for one another. I hope to see you at celebrations across the Commonwealth in the days ahead.
Happy Pride!
Sincerely,
John Moran [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Rep%20Moran%20at%20Pride.png]
State Representative
Suffolk District 9

| **FIRST:** David Trone spent millions running one of the most expensive House races in America.

**THEN:** David Trone spent even more trying to buy a seat in the U.S. Senate.

**Now:** After losing to Angela Alsobrooks, David Trone wants Maryland's 6th District back and expects voters to hand it to him.

After three campaigns and tens of millions of dollars spent, David Trone seems to believe public office is something you can keep buying until it finally belongs to you.

_**I disagree.**_

No one is entitled to represent Maryland’s families. Not because they’re wealthy, not because they’ve run before, and not because they think they can “buy” their way back into office.

Public office is not a consolation prize. It is not a backup plan. And it is not something voters owe anyone. _**It is a responsibility that must be earned.**_

THEN: David Trone spent even more trying to buy a seat in the U.S. Senate. Now: After losing to Angela Alsobrooks, David Trone wants Maryland's 6th District back and expects voters to hand it to him. After three campaigns and tens of millions of dollars spent, David Trone seems to believe public office is something you can keep buying until it finally belongs to you. I disagree. No one is entitled to represent Maryland’s families. Not because they’re wealthy, not because they’ve run before, and not because they think they can “buy” their way back into office. Public office is not a consolation prize. It is not a backup plan. And it is not something voters owe anyone. It is a responsibility that must be earned. I know where I stand. # Anthropic calls for global AI development pause
Artificial intelligence company Anthropic proposed a **[global pause on building the most powerful AI systems,](https://substack.com/redirect/3046d48e-c9c0-4b61-ba6e-a236e3ff0e6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/3046d48e-c9c0-4b61-ba6e-a236e3ff0e6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)warning that latest models show signs they could escape human control.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3046d48e-c9c0-4b61-ba6e-a236e3ff0e6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Worldwide Slowdown Urged:** The San Francisco firm behind Claude models stated a temporary halt in frontier AI development would likely benefit the world by letting societal structures and alignment research catch up.
* **Coordination Mechanism Required:** Effective pause needs major AI companies in the US and China to agree simultaneously under verifiable rules to prevent rivals from racing ahead unchecked.
* **Competitive Pressures Noted:** Without global coordination, companies and governments face difficult safety decisions under competitive and geopolitical pressures from rivals.
* **Recursive Improvement Risk:** Internal data shows AI dramatically accelerating its own development, narrowing the human role and potentially leading to recursive self-improvement sooner than expected.

# Seattle Mayor proposes doubling transit sales tax
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson **[proposed nearly doubling the city's transit sales tax](https://substack.com/redirect/34c704fa-ecc5-4f36-a80f-bb7bf7cd66f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to 0.3 percent to fund bus service improvements and provide free passes to lower-income residents, replacing the expiring 0.15 percent levy with a new 0.3 percent measure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34c704fa-ecc5-4f36-a80f-bb7bf7cd66f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Doubling Sales Tax:** The ten-year proposal would boost Metro bus funding by about 50 percent, supporting around 280,000 trips annually instead of 100,000 and allocating $96 million yearly for all-week services.
* **Free ORCA Passes:** Around 22,000 free transit passes would be distributed to lower-income residents over the decade, more than doubling the current amount.
* **Household Cost Impact:** Median two-person households would pay an additional $29 annually, raising their total transit tax cost to $58 per year.
* **Light Rail Support:** The measure includes $6 million annually for Sound Transit light rail expansions like West Seattle and Ballard Link Extensions.

# Florida homeowners eye $250K property tax exemption
Florida lawmakers passed a constitutional amendment for voter approval that would raise the homestead exemption to $250,000, **[potentially eliminating non-school property taxes for many homeowners,](https://substack.com/redirect/dcef278c-553d-45dc-965a-7c4579550a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** though newcomers face a four-year wait for full benefits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dcef278c-553d-45dc-965a-7c4579550a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Homestead Exemption Rise:** The exemption would increase from $50,000 to $150,000 on January 1, 2027, then to $250,000 in 2028 if approved by voters in November 2026.
* **Newcomer Catch:** Residents establishing primary residency after December 31, 2026, must wait four years to qualify for the full $250,000 exemption.
* **Eligibility For Early:** Those establishing residency on or before December 31, 2026, qualify for the expanded exemption when it takes effect.
* **Assessment Cap Change:** The amendment would also reduce the annual assessment increase cap on non-homestead properties from 10 percent to 5 percent.

# Bitcoin suffers it's ugliest week in months

---|---|---
* **Record ETF Outflows Hit:** Bitcoin ETFs saw 13 straight days of net outflows, reducing total assets to $82.8 billion from $107.8 billion mid-May.

* **Cycle Analysis Persists:** Analysts note four-year crypto cycle suggests potential bottom below $40,000 in late October.

# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2257%2E791427%2EPWId41)
Friend,
My name is Liban Mohamed. I'm the son of two Somali immigrants, and I’m running for Congress in Utah.
I’m also proud to be endorsed by Rep. Ilhan Omar.
In just a moment, I’m going to ask you to [**split a donation between me and Rep. Omar’s campaign for Congress**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-mohamed.6YaM24&refcode=em260605-1-90&t=2&akid=2257%2E791427%2EPWId41) – but before I do, let me explain why our campaign needs your support.
A few weeks ago, I did something most people thought was impossible: **I walked into the Utah Democratic Convention and came out with a win.**
It wasn’t because I had the most money.
It wasn’t because I had the most name recognition.
And it wasn’t because I fit the mold of what a Congressional candidate in Utah traditionally looks like.
**I won the Utah Democratic Convention because we out-organized everyone else in that room.**
For more than five months, our campaign has been doing the unglamorous work that most political campaigns do not.
We’ve been showing up in community centers, in mosques, in immigrant neighborhoods across Salt Lake County – talking to people who have been told, again and again, that their voices don’t matter in Utah politics.
**Well it turns out, when communities like ours organize and demand better, we have the power to change things.**
I’m running for Congress because my community deserves a fighter: I’m an unapologetic Gen Z progressive who is running to end the genocide in Gaza, to abolish ICE, and to make healthcare, housing, and childcare human rights.
We’re building a coalition of Muslim, immigrant, and working voters, alongside so many other groups that have historically been excluded by our politics – and we’re proving that when we move together, we can accomplish great things.
[**But here’s the deal – I’m not taking a cent of corporate PAC money, which means we need grassroots support to continue powering this campaign. Will you split a contribution between my campaign and Rep. We’ve had it.

Senator Fetterman just handed Trump a victory — a blue slip for his crony
judicial nominee Antonio Pozos, clearing the path for yet another Trump
judge to claim a lifetime seat on the bench.

Fetterman had the power to stop this cold. He didn't use it. So we're
making sure every voter in Pennsylvania knows exactly what their senator
just allowed.

Demand Justice is launching a six-figure ad buy putting Fetterman on blast
— and we're drawing a line:

Any Democratic senator who returns a blue slip for one of Trump's
political puppets will face the same. Every single time. No exceptions. No
excuses.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260605-1._kEAnP&refcode=em20260605-61514&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61514%2E1407376%2EPHXxDy ]If that’s all you need to hear, rush a donation now to demand

loyalist nominees.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260605-1._kEAnP&amount=5&refcode=em20260605-61514&t=1004&akid=61514%2E1407376%2EPHXxDy ]Donate $5 ››

Here's why this fight matters: Not one of Trump's judicial nominees is an
independent jurist. Every single one has refused to say who won the 2020
election or refused to acknowledge the January 6th attack on the Capitol.

They're loyalty oath-takers — vetted to rubber-stamp Trump's authoritarian
agenda, not guard the Constitution.

And any senator who acts like these are normal times is deluding
themselves.

If Democrats truly believe they must stand up to Trump's attacks on the
rule of law, they have to do it in every room — not just on Twitter or TV.
In the Judiciary Committee. On the floor. And with every blue slip that
crosses their desk.

No crony judges. No complicit senators. Full stop.

We need the resources to keep up this fight. Holding senators accountable
takes real work — and right now, we need you.

name: Kathryn Harvey
subject: 🎂Tomorrow is my birthday...
body:
📣Go vote early by 5pm today!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/8bfe3b360a64/kathryn-harvey-for-congresscampaign-kickoff-6426323?e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
|
---
| | **Tune-in June 9 to Fox Carolina for Election Night coverage with yours truly from 6 to 8pm and 10pm to midnight.**
---
| |
# Tomorrow I turn 44 years old
---
|
---
| | And what a trip around the sun it’s been. I chose this photo, first and foremost, because I’m surrounded by many of the women (but certainly not all of them) that I’ve been building with personally, professionally, and politically for years. And it has occurred to me as of late, that my measure of success these days are the depth and breadth of my female friendships. I had someone that I respect and admire asked me this week if I had good friends. I replied, “Yes, many of them actually, from every part of my life.” And she followed up, “How do you have time for them?” To which I replied, “I make time. In fact, I prioritize the women in my life who lift me up every single day, over almost anything else.” It felt important to acknowledge this as another trip starts.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
# If you’ve been keeping up with me, you know it’s been a busy one.
---
| |
This year, I’ve had the pleasure of leading communication efforts for the [Spartanburg 250 Revolutionary War Committee](https://us.list-manage.com/dOJiB5uAX2v?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a), joining the [Frogmore Stew Podcast](https://us.list-manage.com/JoLdAH4y4_n?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a) as the Upstate host and supporting our first Content Creators & Candidates Summit, rolling out the first of its kind [statewide voter guide for South Carolina](https://us.list-manage.com/G8vUpXHRn6J?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a), Recruiting a [dozen candidates ](https://us.list-manage.com/vMpHfPkTPbU?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)to run in Spartanburg County in my fifth year as party chair, launching the inaugural [Red & Blue Summit in Spartanburg](https://us.list-manage.com/QBeCNeHli1x?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a) featuring Gov. Lujan Grishom of New Mexico, Sen. Joni Ernst of Iowa, Congresswoman Lauren Underwood of Illinois and more.
But most importantly, I’ve had the privilege to continue building towards a better South Carolina with so many of you. So this birthday, I’m going to ask for a small contribution to Support the South Carolina Voter Guide efforts. [_**Consider it a bday gift for democracy!**_](https://us.list-manage.com/TbMB6CLs3gm?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Zey2MxMzteJ?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
| |
This is a non-partisan guide built with information available on the public profiles of each candidate. The guide is a project of an Upstate organization, [Responsible Action](https://us.list-manage.com/19cR5GgDvNz?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a) whose mission is to promote good governance, transparency, and voter education. [**Support the SC Voter Guide today!**](https://us.list-manage.com/wv_ilmNkJIJ?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
| [Support the Voter Guide ](https://us.list-manage.com/jqkybYQy7Q_?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
|
---
| |
# Recruiting candidates to run in every state house seat in Spartanburg County.
---
| | This year we have nine candidates challenging Republican incumbents in Spartanburg County State House seats...and they are all formidable. I’ve never been more proud of a group who stepped up to ensure their neighbors have choice on the ballot, their current elected officials are held accountable, and they help turn out voters for the top of the ticket this year. And you can support all of them with one contribution to our [Local Champions Fund. ](https://us.list-manage.com/Rx537ygD6lr?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/USkEVqpUa8r?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
| [Support our candidates today!](https://us.list-manage.com/VAzQB66KoNr?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)
---
|
---
| |
# The First of it’s kind Content Creators Summit x Candidate Summit launched last week in SC
---
| | The team at [Frogmore Stew Media & Slay Strategies ](https://us.list-manage.com/KYtXoWg23gE?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)collaborated to launch a SC Content Creators Summit and Candidate Summit before the Democratic Convention last Friday. And it was everything we dreamed it could be. A dozen creators and twenty five candidates came together for a day of training, collaborating and connecting. We all needed it! Shout out to Grace Cowan for leading the charge and Kate Barr for sharing the blue print.
---

---
| |

* **Democratic ballots:** 108,637
* **Republican ballots:** 49,334

**As of Tuesday in Spartanburg County** 9,797 have voted early.
* **Democratic ballots:** 4,710

**Kristina Knickerbocker** , running to flip Ohio’s 10th Congressional District, is an Air Force veteran and nurse who worked multiple jobs to put herself through school.

**Sarah Trone Garriott** , running to flip Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District, is a minister, a mom, and the daughter of a nurse and an auto mechanic who worked at Walmart, waited tables, and cleaned hotel rooms to pay for college.

**Kaela Berg** , running for Minnesota’s 2nd Congressional District, is a union flight attendant who has worked multiple jobs at once.

**Rebecca Cooke** , running to flip Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, is a longtime waitress and daughter of dairy farmers who still takes diner shifts between campaign stops.

**Keisha Lance Bottoms** , running to flip the Georgia governor’s office, is a fifth-generation Georgian, mom of four, and former Atlanta mayor who is fighting to lower costs and deliver for working families across Georgia.

**Deb Haaland** , running for governor of New Mexico, is a single mom who relied on food stamps and sold homemade salsa to make ends meet while raising her daughter.

**_And then there are the badass women who have already served their country in uniform — and are now stepping up to keep serving in office:_**

**JoAnna Mendoza** , running to flip Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, served in the Navy and Marine Corps. **Rebecca Bennett** , running to flip New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District, is a former Navy helicopter pilot.

**Jessica Killin** , running to flip Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, served as an Army captain and paratrooper. **Leela Gray** , running to flip Florida’s 13th Congressional District, is a retired Army brigadier general. **Nancy Lacore** , running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District, worked her way through the Naval ranks to eventually serve as the Chief of the Navy Reserve, entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors.

These women have served their country. They have worked for a paycheck. They have cared for their families and communities. And now, they are running to represent people whose lives reflect the same struggles they’ve experienced firsthand.

This is why electing women matters so much this cycle, Peter.

The women EMILYs List supports are not running because politics is easy. They are running because their communities need leaders who understand what working families are actually up against — and who are ready to fight for them.

But even the strongest candidates cannot win alone.

clean_body: | = We knew that would get your attention. Now, Peter, let us introduce you to a few women who should have it instead. Women who are veterans. Women who have working-class backgrounds. Women who are caregivers, small business owners, public servants, and leaders. They know what it means to stretch a dollar, make hard choices, serve their communities, and fight for the people counting on them. That is not just a compelling biography. It is a strong electoral strategy. Democrats need candidates who can speak directly to voters who feel ignored, squeezed, and written off. = | = Kristina Knickerbocker , running to flip Ohio’s 10th Congressional District, is an Air Force veteran and nurse who worked multiple jobs to put herself through school. Sarah Trone Garriott , running to flip Iowa’s 3rd Congressional District, is a minister, a mom, and the daughter of a nurse and an auto mechanic who worked at Walmart, waited tables, and cleaned hotel rooms to pay for college. Kaela Berg , running for Minnesota’s 2nd Congressional District, is a union flight attendant who has worked multiple jobs at once. Rebecca Cooke , running to flip Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, is a longtime waitress and daughter of dairy farmers who still takes diner shifts between campaign stops. Keisha Lance Bottoms , running to flip the Georgia governor’s office, is a fifth-generation Georgian, mom of four, and former Atlanta mayor who is fighting to lower costs and deliver for working families across Georgia. Deb Haaland , running for governor of New Mexico, is a single mom who relied on food stamps and sold homemade salsa to make ends meet while raising her daughter. And then there are the badass women who have already served their country in uniform — and are now stepping up to keep serving in office: JoAnna Mendoza , running to flip Arizona’s 6th Congressional District, served in the Navy and Marine Corps. Rebecca Bennett , running to flip New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District, is a former Navy helicopter pilot. Jessica Killin , running to flip Colorado’s 5th Congressional District, served as an Army captain and paratrooper. Leela Gray , running to flip Florida’s 13th Congressional District, is a retired Army brigadier general. Nancy Lacore , running to flip South Carolina's 1st Congressional District, worked her way through the Naval ranks to eventually serve as the Chief of the Navy Reserve, entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors. These women have served their country. They have worked for a paycheck. They have cared for their families and communities. And now, they are running to represent people whose lives reflect the same struggles they’ve experienced firsthand. This is why electing women matters so much this cycle, Peter. The women EMILYs List supports are not running because politics is easy. They are running because their communities need leaders who understand what working families are actually up against — and who are ready to fight for them. # DNC NextWave Regional Bootcamp in Pittsburgh, PA!
---
| | Are you a current or aspiring campaign or state party staffer in the Eastern United States looking to take your career to the next level and help ensure Democrats win up and down the ballot in November?
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/yW11TMpGY2q?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
| |

**The DNC is seeking campaign professionals in the East to participate in the NextWave Eastern Regional Bootcamp in Pittsburgh, PA, Wednesday, June 24 – Friday, June 26**. This three-day, in-person intensive training program prepares the next generation of campaign and state party professionals for the 2026 cycle and beyond. This program is **FREE** to attend, and will provide NextWave graduates with invaluable professional development opportunities both during and after the program.
Participants will be placed in one of two tracks based on their experience with professional campaign work:
1. **Campaigns 101** : for current or aspiring field organizers, fellows, and campaign associates with less than two cycles of experience who are looking to strengthen their skills and get exposure to new aspects of campaign and state party work. No previous experience with campaign work is required!
2. **Management Track** : for mid-level and senior campaign and state party professionals who understand the technical aspects of campaign work but are looking to expand their skills as managers and leaders in the Democratic ecosystem.

[**Learn More and Apply to the DNC NextWave Eastern Regional Bootcamp Here**](https://us.list-manage.com/watT0L3Z4qZ?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)**.** Spots for the program are limited.**** Applications will be considered on a rolling basis, and early applications are encouraged. **The application will be open until Sunday, June 14, at 11:59 p.m. ET.**
*Live outside of the East but want to participate in a future NextWave Bootcamp? Sign up for the [**DNC Training Department Newsletter**](https://us.list-manage.com/IFEenKy59lZ?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) to hear when the next bootcamps are announced.

| | | | | This is serious...

I'm hearing that some Republicans are getting complacent. Voters seem to think now that we've won the White House, they can just sit on the sidelines...

| | | | | |
---
[ ](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=5ed8b15103b846bcba48f9d064517c25&_e=hAvsty7Yj-3KI1WGH6tZpf0IYPJFAFI6FfNLXhEFwwVGOpDefVCI7jcYSPd-2WIseols_iindJ5LmcHsXB669maWIVt3ai4YCCyyd2n5Mg6hH61RLnGxmb2Q8x0dHegkd7Fqpv8o1K-Zl8npf_YrFgpQ-QClpVLvuee-Es1xNLuwSrJq6zqaPgewlE3eK8EP-pKA-b3vbaSVlP13d-fDIpLIg9CHjn2Y2ZKD6reloYgalGnUXtNvLfdoPN6GihDmNf57OL0df2myvhbNjH3GmwShPnsmqUn2t9Axa_nJunldzjD5dc-3BA7uzVQ9QJ3hDCY5QBqZIfOK7kElg26xu2DqU7M7g-ESB3VQDtvCfL_kHcxXxWcC9N1ky4X0wovMPKqgNcFRnfBYEknq3rH-bD3SQjCUcSSnWnVxu2CHZHXM8TppJsT2qSoLg3bknzG--_ZRZmQQxxo2OLfqhg_m3PO6Xh9GlcbbJFpMs3G5HUMg6E6PJ6LoVxcuP4qhjqnCIe1-r0T9mVfY5m_mb4KeVQyZdctilXy3gUDQhpBJjMCR1N85IIJX9LAAQLMKkyVvkurc6eQ9RsaqQM8_vj5olclgCFGuQdjAuqJ6an7vtUOXkMoEGlJ5pNEsSgCjRd_c0oFMDRlxwJ3lf9fFTm8_bI29jHht0Gj_j6U__0S2qx0wdXLSp86VM-vgFCPhKFu4)

Friend,
"Abby" was missing. Her mother had done everything right and was getting nowhere. Nobody was helping. In her words, she was flabbergasted and lost, terrified for her daughter, with no idea what to do next.
**That is the moment most people never see, and the moment Heroes for Humanity was built for.**
We sent operators in. They started surveillance, built intelligence on the ground, and narrowed the search to a single area. Within 24 hours of our operator arriving, we had a confirmed sighting.
Shortly after, he picked her up, called her mother, notified local police, and brought her home.
**Her mother said it plainly: without our team, nothing would have happened. It would have stayed exactly as it was, or gotten far worse.**
I want to be honest with you about why this is so rare.
You can likely count on one hand the number of nonprofits in this country that actually go hands-on – that physically go in and bring a child out. Most cannot.
**The backbone of Heroes for Humanity is veteran special operators trained to find people who do not want to be found, anywhere in the world.** We use those same skills to find missing and trafficked children, here at home and abroad, and to physically return them to their families.
"Abby" is one story among many. We recovered **9 children in California in 2023** , identified more than **8 trafficked children** in our work last year, and brought home **three more teenagers from trafficking situations in Virginia and West Texas** this past January. Each one is a name, a face, a family. And each one is the reason the next call cannot go unanswered.
_And trafficking is only one front._ The same operators who find these children went behind enemy lines to bring families home from Afghanistan, stood up evacuations in active war zones in the Middle East, and put food in the hands of a thousand people a day in Zambia – all while carrying the Gospel into the darkest places on earth.
**Precision rescue, humanitarian aid, and the hope of Jesus Christ. That is the whole of who we are.**
---
---
**My name is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments, writing to you as Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity. **We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Today we are a 501(c)(3) network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work in the trenches that most organizations cannot.

I am proud to represent Oregon’s 6th Congressional District and fight for the best interests of Oregonians in Congress. Change can happen in a generation. **I know because it happened to me.**
Let me explain:
When my dad was five years old, he immigrated from Mexico to Texas. He picked cotton and tomatoes in the fields of the Rio Grande Valley, all the while dreaming that one day he would work his way out of poverty and make it to the middle class.
My parents taught me the value of hard work. And I grew up believing that if we worked hard, anything was possible.
But when I got to college, I realized my parents didn’t have the money to pay for my tuition and their groceries. So I worked all kinds of odd jobs to put myself through school. It took seven years, but I finished my degree and became the first person in my family to graduate from college.
When my daughter was born, I felt in my core the same determination that drove my parents: **there was nothing that would keep me from doing everything in my power to shape a stronger, more equitable future for Amelia and her generation.**
But right now, Washington is being run by Donald Trump and his MAGA majority, who are, quite frankly, willing to purposefully tank our economy if it means their party can get ahead.
They have pushed reckless tariffs and launched us into a new war that has caused gas and grocery prices to skyrocket, passed a reckless budget bill that ripped away healthcare from hundreds of thousands of Americans, and cut funding for programs our communities rely on.
Families are doing _everything_ right, but are still struggling to get by. We deserve better.

Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.

This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
