News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]
* Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections/assistant/]
* Everything you need to know about mail voting [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-mail-ballot-how-to-request-fill-out-return] , becoming a poll worker [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide]
* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]
* Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-commonwealth-superior-court-candidates] , vetting judicial candidates [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-candidate-vetting-guide]
* Guides to State College school board [https://www.spotlightpa.org/statecollege/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-state-college-school-board-anderson-huff-barlow-black-desmarais-mcternan-sogor] , Reading City Council president [https://www.spotlightpa.org/berks/2025/04/reading-city-council-president-primary-election-2025]
* Guides to voting as a college student [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-college-student-voting-guide]
En Español
* Guía para votar por correo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pensilvania-elecciones-primarias-2025-votar-correo-como-llenar] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/reading-concejo-municipal-primarias-elecciones-2025]
* Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-primarias-elecciones-2025-votar-informacion] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-elecciones-2025-como-convertirse-trabajador-electoral]
2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:
Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/advocacy-groups-offer-training-for-pa-primary-poll-watchers/]
Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide/]
Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [https://fcfreepresspa.com/poll-workers-needed-for-pennsylvanias-2025-primary-election/]
6. Engage Your Elected Officials
Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.
7. Vote in Every Election
Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. Upcoming events As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls. [] Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students. Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader. With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] [] Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot. Your vote shapes our justice system! Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms. When: Monday, May 12, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] Social Media of the Week [] The deadline to request your mail-in ballot for the primary election is May 13th at 5PM. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [] The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests. In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [] . [] We are hiring! Let's provide civic education together! We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania. Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote! Positions start at $20 an hour. Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org] EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org] News You Can Use There are things every one of us can do [] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last. 1. Educate Yourself Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally. Stay Engaged To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win. Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [] ) 3. Share What You Learn Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting. Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year! 4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work. Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above! 5. Become a Trained Poll Worker Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process. Engage Your Elected Officials Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise. 7. Vote in Every Election Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility. Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list -- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote.

RUSH $35 or more right now to help inform voters of this change and defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [] Voter Action Project [] HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [] Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list -- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote. Peter Willis,

Maine’s primary is just DAYS away – and super PACs fueled by secretive
ultra-wealthy donors are FLOODING the state to defend their political turf
and attack Our Revolution-backed champions for the working class.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34620?source=email-20260605v&t=1055&akid=10846%2E5885482%2EAr-Rtl ]Headline: Super PACs should be outlawed, says Platner, as pro-Collins
corporate dark money pours into Maine to Attack him

Senate candidate Graham Platner is calling out what’s happening:
billionaires and corporations are drowning out the voices of working
people so the rich can stay in charge.

It’s happening in real time as Platner’s campaign is being barraged with
$2 MILLION in attack ads – and he isn’t the only target. The Democratic
establishment is spending big to stop progressives in other races too, but
the good news is we have something more powerful: 73,000 Our Revolution
supporters in every corner of Maine, rural and urban alike.

The outcome in Maine in November could be the deciding factor in whether
we flip the Senate blue. But that’s just the beginning.

Matt Dunlap – Bernie’s 2016 state co-chair and Maine’s longest-serving
Secretary of State – is running for Congress in Maine’s 2nd District. The
DCCC is actively working to stop him from winning the primary, throwing
weight behind an establishment Democrat instead, but Matt is refusing to
back down – and Our Revolution is standing with him.

Then there’s Troy Jackson, who is running for Governor. He’s a logger and
union leader, fighting alongside workers on the picket line for decades,
and that terrifies the billionaires and political establishment on both
sides. But PACs have already spent $8.6 million in the governor’s primary
alone – closing in on the *entire* outside spending from the last election
for Governor.

We always knew that CA-27 was a difficult district to win. It's why until last cycle, it was the last Republican-held seat in all of Los Angeles County.

We've already faced national GOP attacks and outside spending. In 2024, over _$15 million_ was spent to defeat me. Now, we need to prepare for what's to come as we work to defend this seat for the first time – with new challenges including redrawn district lines.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | What are you hiding in Fremont Elon??? # Federal Administration Provides $85 Million to Reopen Warrior Run Electric Plant in Western Maryland.
---
|
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/2Vj3EMIbOHn?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
---
| | Click the image or this link to watch the Facebook live press conference:
[https://www.facebook.com/share/v/14f73M4WDYX/?mibextid=wwXIfr](https://us.list-manage.com/7NZEXs3fLkO?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
---
| [RUSH YOUR DONATION NOW FOR OUR NEXT REPORT](https://us.list-manage.com/AVE769tftFg?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b "RUSH YOUR DONATION NOW FOR OUR NEXT REPORT")
---
| Dear Dan Cox for Governor,

Four years ago today, on June 4th, I stood right here in Western Maryland while campaigning for Governor and announced our Project Not Forgotten initiative. I warned that under a Wes Moore administration, Warrior Run power plant would be closed. And that is exactly what happened - and not just Warrior Run, but he has scheduled Brandon Shore and Wagner power plants to also close, destabilizing our grid and skyrocketing our electric costs all in teh name of failed "green energy" wind and solar policies.

Our message was simple: _no part of Maryland would be forgotten_.

Not Western Maryland.

Not the Eastern Shore.

Not Southern Maryland.

Not the working families who have watched politicians in Annapolis take their jobs, raise their taxes, and ignore their communities.

We pledged to fight for all of Maryland.

_Today, standing here again on June 4th, we are seeing proof that the fight was worth it. And the Western Maryland delegation and Senator McKay and all those who fought for this deserve credit for their work._

**The President and his Administration is taking decisive action to direct approximately $85 million in Defense Production Act funding toward reopening the Warrior Run Power Plant in Western Maryland.**

This is a major victory for Maryland workers, Maryland families, and Maryland energy independence.

For years, Maryland politicians have pursued policies that shut down reliable power generation while forcing families to pay higher and higher electric bills.

They told us reliability didn’t matter.

They told us affordability would follow.

They were wrong.

Marylanders are paying the price every month when they open their utility bills.

Warrior Run was Maryland’s last operating coal-fired power plant. It provided more than 200 megawatts of reliable, around-the-clock electricity generation. It generated enough power for well over 100,000 homes while helping maintain stability throughout Western Maryland and the broader PJM electric grid.

The value of Warrior Run cannot be measured simply by percentages or statistics.

Reliable power is the foundation of economic growth.

Reliable power is the foundation of national security.

Reliable power is the foundation of family budget security.

Without affordable and dependable electricity, businesses cannot grow, manufacturers cannot compete, and families cannot thrive.

_Today, the Federal Government is stepping in where Governor Moore has failed_.

While Annapolis has focused on ideological energy policies, Maryland families have been left with rising costs and increasing uncertainty about our energy future.

This federal action demonstrates what real leadership looks like.

It means jobs.

It means investment.

It means energy security.

And it means hope for Western Maryland. And for all of Maryland.

As Governor, I will fight to bring Maryland’s power generation back online, strengthen our electric grid, protect ratepayers, and restore the reliable infrastructure that built this state.

Maryland should be producing more energy, not less.

Maryland should be lowering electric bills, not raising them.

Maryland should be leading, not falling behind.

Four years ago, we promised that Western Maryland would not be forgotten.

Today, that promise is being fulfilled.

Thank you, God bless Western Maryland, and God bless the great State of Maryland.

We will win this race, but I need your support to do so. Please [donate today ](https://us.list-manage.com/Z6NMwSFz523?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)and sign up to volunteer at a polling location near you at DanCoxforGovernor.com.

For Common Sense, Freedom and Maryland,

Dan Cox
Candidate for Governor

Authority Dan Cox for Governor; Nick Krop, CPA, Treasurer.

Together, we have the chance to make history by electing the first Native American woman Governor in the country. But more than that, we have the chance to protect and build a New Mexico where working families can actually get ahead.

That’s why I’m so determined to fight for lower costs, build stronger schools to get kids reading earlier, expand and strengthen access to healthcare, and foster safer communities.
_But this won’t be easy._
_As you read this,_ Republicans are watching to see if we have what it takes to stop them from bringing Trump’s dangerous and extremist agenda to New Mexico. They’re prepared to spend millions to flip this seat.

We just made history!

Thanks to thousands of small-dollar donations, countless volunteer hours spent talking to voters, and the shared belief that Montanans deserve better – **I am now the official Democratic nominee for MT-01, and we are one step closer to making sure Congress delivers for working people.**

Now, the real work begins.

In these next five months, we’re going to take our message to every corner of the district. Democrats have real work to do to win back working people’s trust. I know this because as a union leader and smokejumper, I’ve worked alongside the folks we’ve been losing.

So we’re going to do things differently. We’re going to keep showing up everywhere, having the hard conversations, and building an undefeatable coalition come November.

**[Colorado protected school funding without touching TABOR refunds. Now it wants those too.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Last session, the Colorado General Assembly passed a bill asking voters to waive their TABOR refunds to fund education.
The ballot title calls it “without raising taxes.” No rates change.
But it asks Coloradans to let the state keep money the constitution currently requires it to give back, and it comes one year after the legislature moved more than $200 million into a protected school account without touching anyone’s refund at all.
The two moves address the same problem. They work very differently.

**[Xcel Customers Face Largest Electric Rate Hike In Colorado History](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **A proposed $225 million settlement would raise the average household bill nearly 6% to $110.81 a month:** the deal is opposed by the Office of Utility Consumer Advocate, AARP Colorado, and the city of Boulder, who argue residential customers are being saddled with costs driven by corporate interests and legislatively mandated green energy programs.
* **Xcel originally sought $355 million, citing $4 billion in investments and a 67% rise in construction costs:** but consumer advocates argue the utility is forcing customers to pay for shareholder profits — including charges for the Comanche 3 coal plant in Pueblo, which has been offline since last August.
* **Utility rate hike approvals have climbed sharply — regulators now approve 64% of requests compared to 52% historically:** with Colorado families already absorbing a 28% rate increase over three years, opponents are asking the PUC to reject the settlement and proceed with hearings set to begin June 11.

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[FAIR FOR ALL](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **A taxpayer-funded parks district now classifies "deliberate use of the wrong pronouns" as harassment:** meaning a woman who voices discomfort about undressing alongside a biological male in a locker room risks a discrimination claim under the district's updated policy.

* **The policy flows from Colorado's HB 25-1312, which treats chosen names and pronouns as protected "gender expression":** constitutional scholar Jonathan Turley has called Colorado "arguably the most anti-free speech state in the union," noting the state repeatedly passes compelled speech laws only to lose in federal court.

* **Legal organization FAIR has put the district on notice that forcing employees to affirm beliefs they don't hold violates the First Amendment:** Boll says she will treat everyone with professionalism, but will not be compelled by her government employer to speak words she does not believe.

My grandfather worked long days as a Mexican farmworker, and my single mom sacrificed everything to raise two kids on her own.| | | | I never thought I'd make it this far in the first place.

But the LORD works in mysterious ways.

Growing up, my family struggled to make ends meet. My grandfather worked long days as a Mexican farmworker, and my single mom sacrificed everything to raise two kids on her own. I remember the many hours I spent washing dishes just to put myself through school. _We didn't have much, but we had our faith and our determination._

When I decided to run for Congress in 2020, people thought I was crazy. No Republican had EVER won our seat, and the Democrats had all the money and connections. But I knew I had to try. I couldn't just sit back - not when the stakes were so high. _We came within 3 points of pulling off the unthinkable ... but it wasn't enough. _

**We lost. And it felt like a punch to the gut.** It was one of the hardest things I've ever had to accept. And I could've gone back to the life I had built for myself. But that wasn't where I was going to be at the end of my story. I refused to give up. I prayed for guidance and the strength to keep going.

And in 2022, I decided to run again. The odds were still against me but I kept the faith, and on election night...

We won in a historic upset, and it was like the whole world had been turned upside down.

The far-Left had controlled our district for so long, and they couldn't believe that a Conservative Latina had won it. But with that victory came a new challenge.

My grandfather worked long days as a Mexican farmworker, and my single mom sacrificed everything to raise two kids on her own.| | | | I never thought I'd make it this far in the first place. But the LORD works in mysterious ways. Growing up, my family struggled to make ends meet. My grandfather worked long days as a Mexican farmworker, and my single mom sacrificed everything to raise two kids on her own. I remember the many hours I spent washing dishes just to put myself through school. We didn't have much, but we had our faith and our determination. When I decided to run for Congress in 2020, people thought I was crazy. No Republican had EVER won our seat, and the Democrats had all the money and connections. But I knew I had to try. I couldn't just sit back - not when the stakes were so high. We came within 3 points of pulling off the unthinkable ... but it wasn't enough. We lost. And it felt like a punch to the gut. It was one of the hardest things I've ever had to accept. And I could've gone back to the life I had built for myself. But that wasn't where I was going to be at the end of my story. I refused to give up. I prayed for guidance and the strength to keep going. And in 2022, I decided to run again. The odds were still against me but I kept the faith, and on election night... We won in a historic upset, and it was like the whole world had been turned upside down. The far-Left had controlled our district for so long, and they couldn't believe that a Conservative Latina had won it. But with that victory came a new challenge. This year, the top Democrat Super PAC already pledged $50 million to take me down and win back the House for the Liberals. | | | | I'm not just fighting for my seat; I'm fighting to deliver President Turmp's entire Conservative agenda. So if you can spare a few bucks, it will make all the difference in the world. We CANNOT surrender this critical seat to the Democrats - they see it as their golden ticket back to House control. subject: What To Know About The American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act
body:

body:
A girl named "Abby" was missing. Her mother had done everything right and was getting nowhere.

| | | | | |
---
[ ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d8ea7b8c190341779156c81ca9db7eb4&_e=rFvUW9unPCVAePVDa0JBVv31_Jw3SrFScvLbrHTAC2AOwT2HYbTSKq5P7ljIs1zn85MDEXuCLuk-SQSbEKgZlt-vuTJWDahR4EMhAcNtjagmptP6mEgTBxF-u0iOnGlwd62cjv8lbrRUku6CC_-W83ogLS8SKJ3It71N-iYIcRnhZkhBaxvZzU6IyklfFnjdAtzuz-q4gC_Zs8D66l8Jk0t80V_loWJSKYDS-WvIOGJaGMbm9iwDq6lOxrE0Z3qAzNeR8pBQfLl9NtVRyXJGB5FwfhSIQBY7wcRha6dshJoWoeiD8vAf6Ks3nOhsX2ldweg00tR0WedDlPUDh3l0hwPQFlWdSd5dsBVDmcvyEF0tP6HaKvj8N7az9ZNbTI43M3y6-i2-Fts-wPAoZpxHU__wQzic6qHheT2KbvzQalM-mzmF_vCXzagHuwHZgmwW7ISUP629o2nx37h0dXnxCnoFJFTVXsXK70bmCL2CP28PeUYBCLEgltIknY9zMAcQZspfU_Z82udGkYg2heL34uaL9yE-4G_3_RE3tl7Vpr3nEeDH_W8Rw35FgO7iEtPDsG6kudykgukg6aKk6_N4C6wlOW0lqyZddkntvlJdchKBtPzQpJ6JPwYmfmEQXt4YuKWtSlCQKdd9aHQjbeufE6FCTmSm9HAedwPY_hQw_BWFqMg57fOAgRwSWqt6ufQo)
---
Friend,
"Abby" was missing. Her mother had done everything right and was getting nowhere. Nobody was helping. In her words, she was flabbergasted and lost, terrified for her daughter, with no idea what to do next.
**That is the moment most people never see, and the moment Heroes for Humanity was built for.**
We sent operators in. They started surveillance, built intelligence on the ground, and narrowed the search to a single area. Within 24 hours of our operator arriving, we had a confirmed sighting.
Shortly after, he picked her up, called her mother, notified local police, and brought her home.
**Her mother said it plainly: without our team, nothing would have happened. It would have stayed exactly as it was, or gotten far worse.**
I want to be honest with you about why this is so rare.
You can likely count on one hand the number of nonprofits in this country that actually go hands-on – that physically go in and bring a child out. Most cannot.
**The backbone of Heroes for Humanity is veteran special operators trained to find people who do not want to be found, anywhere in the world.** We use those same skills to find missing and trafficked children, here at home and abroad, and to physically return them to their families.
"Abby" is one story among many. We recovered **9 children in California in 2023** , identified more than **8 trafficked children** in our work last year, and brought home **three more teenagers from trafficking situations in Virginia and West Texas** this past January. Each one is a name, a face, a family. And each one is the reason the next call cannot go unanswered.
_And trafficking is only one front._ The same operators who find these children went behind enemy lines to bring families home from Afghanistan, stood up evacuations in active war zones in the Middle East, and put food in the hands of a thousand people a day in Zambia – all while carrying the Gospel into the darkest places on earth.
**Precision rescue, humanitarian aid, and the hope of Jesus Christ. That is the whole of who we are.**
---
---
**My name is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments, writing to you as Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity. **We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Today we are a 501(c)(3) network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work in the trenches that most organizations cannot.
[ **I’d like to ask you to directly support these critical efforts, but I also want to pull back the curtain a bit to share with you exactly how this all works.** ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d8ea7b8c190341779156c81ca9db7eb4&_e=rFvUW9unPCVAePVDa0JBVv31_Jw3SrFScvLbrHTAC2AOwT2HYbTSKq5P7ljIs1zn85MDEXuCLuk-SQSbEKgZlt-vuTJWDahR4EMhAcNtjagmptP6mEgTBxF-u0iOnGlwd62cjv8lbrRUku6CC_-W83ogLS8SKJ3It71N-iYIcRnhZkhBaxvZzU6IyklfFnjdAtzuz-q4gC_Zs8D66l8Jk0t80V_loWJSKYDS-WvIOGKGjX7Wlz2aIUdaY11NiXkj2t16JinBP8MtefDDI1huvK0JNdB9H7b0H5QNLLBFH3aMW4Zt-YvmAbgAU6Dg9Sl_BGBDaPsCNwzNXlilRCigUKir70T56GK8jz18ja_lqBHKoYRDVgdhAMNHNa-Y5w41P7Gmaqj9valmYnhDpukAX35BSUg4BWkjcktYT7KRhQ9yWnRjdqyaoCWBGnD45dEzbrnEWwWssI_FXwAvySUGJZ2uaOcQprwQfDalU6ouF2STg0OU4hDNNgcu85LlJF6nLakGcwPOo8SsbQMp38KfEekzdhhGY-Z6V44CsAKjE0AuZTIGt5XV4Hf8Z-dGaW0FCvd_SqEuy6aLwZuScfR3k9ZxtmmSrqTIDOhGEor7Of-APwc5RZB5y5OBdvtBnVRGTuxCtecVGtRU8w5vZZh6gfRiBj8kTdUAa-qGJVRnCXZBBuzXej_UF0jUDoTpxg4x) We've put together a short video, with an intro from my dear friend Chad Robichaux, that gets into the tactics, the operators, and the full story of how we brought "Abby" home. [ **Watch it here >>** ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d8ea7b8c190341779156c81ca9db7eb4&_e=rFvUW9unPCVAePVDa0JBVv31_Jw3SrFScvLbrHTAC2AOwT2HYbTSKq5P7ljIs1zn85MDEXuCLuk-SQSbEKgZlt-vuTJWDahR4EMhAcNtjagmptP6mEgTBxF-u0iOnGlwd62cjv8lbrRUku6CC_-W83ogLS8SKJ3It71N-iYIcRnhZkhBaxvZzU6IyklfFnjdAtzuz-q4gC_Zs8D66l8Jk0t80V_loWJSKYDS-WvIOGIc2bx_D8gwsWEHhLufa4TE1-1OSaZv9K_wYByFR_rtK2upI1XhfHI1WxosEYmS9Fe2dgVY_CtGCMaNZ4tjKY6C406CC2B3ROEANPqlwcuh5q_9xeAEBkkG9V-Lwjb1T-9qwudIrrD_uqiJng8vlwFAYsRn8js21Lk1fcB-edmFc8GU7PevZ-Us-3tx4DmM2pIXaA5jmCWnh5CtX7tPwrNfDQ-7ElFuKrDhBSevl6D0bSzlr_Uaa7e--EffSC9ZJ3WaERH-jjYtWee9pWKxeKyzoPIJDaCQsYNgX_vhYt9JG_PfCKWX8qJffbEP5sVeiOF8820rSZmDyny34PXKmb_JaMvgAUKpCkVGzLPYAiyxJcvOa0rUClhoK_peMvp6fq35CwYPqJZc48Eb8dvinlBYSWq7HFXz7eeQTgblNMYiRmIyk2Uy-XsvfHgMusiyuxxX-qZrtS3g_7ljldHegvYx)
**And know this, when you give today, you’re not just funding some generic mission. You’re directly funding tangible programs.** Right now, the two that are front and center are as follows:
**➡️ Our July operator course. **This July we launch the next course in our training pipeline, where candidates are vetted under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure and trained in the fieldcraft, intelligence work, and crisis response the mission demands. This is where operators are made. Rescues like the one you just read about do not happen without it.
**➡️ The National Training Center. **For five years we've done this work from temporary facilities, borrowed space, and on-the-fly logistics. We made it work because we had to. But demand keeps accelerating, and we cannot train operators fast enough this way. So we're building a permanent home for the mission in our home state of Texas – standardized certification for every operator we field, medical and trauma training for austere environments, an intelligence and mission-planning hub, and the capacity to train the next generation at scale.
**Long story short, your gift today funds the brick and mortar place, and the training, that puts the right person in the field when the next call comes.**
[ **A donation of any amount would be a true blessing – even $25. The next missing child is already out there. Please, help us be ready.** ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=d8ea7b8c190341779156c81ca9db7eb4&_e=rFvUW9unPCVAePVDa0JBVv31_Jw3SrFScvLbrHTAC2AOwT2HYbTSKq5P7ljIs1zn85MDEXuCLuk-SQSbEKgZlt-vuTJWDahR4EMhAcNtjagmptP6mEgTBxF-u0iOnGlwd62cjv8lbrRUku6CC_-W83ogLS8SKJ3It71N-iYIcRnhZkhBaxvZzU6IyklfFnjdAtzuz-q4gC_Zs8D66l8Jk0t80V_loWJSKYDS-WvIOGISktGDKnM7L7PwW9jFuhUHNvOae80kF4MtF-bjfrZa7ZrXQLBZ8ecgyyYQZvgUbQTIwIACVSWxbdxHlEB-We3QwuyDELdgnvATtlqNCXWiP4Akg239Xk1c8v-mZDvpnniCl8o6k9wwpu4tpbKumDimw1WK_lLe0BWCOqWAK56FLOxpII8SlZ5D4WBad14h8EEJfwroJJTavFG-mQcgVYBKL75FXFQEbIBzgOO0URFA_ok49wUKtZVZvUOYtjiEEkOOi4emSAAPvmUX9DuSprRwt2z5dmQWVeov-W_tuciIn9MQwFHU-K_e2DuKUyyqqUPESxVcudV7U3RcqrW-FGRufEKi5Bnop00DFoNR3jC8hVJpv0uFGu319AqLLk_iscNfyLAvuCHe_5Mvy2Xx25k_oxok0a26OGJaZcr_Qf9gRMGcJ5vgNLteq8Fe99haeKlOxrjgN_fDs0IuK6llTJew)
Thank you, and let's never forget our mission – to free the oppressed, so others may live.

Dennis Price Founder & CEO Heroes for Humanity

body:
Counteracting Classroom Propaganda
Son of 1776 needs your support to reach millions of young Americans with the true story of America's founding.
[ ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=5d89c365059f46ca9fa52af9bbde43d6&_e=FuBDkzLy9qvh70NJmmyEWCrZn6mZGXmDqThs51FpcMSN1QF1VjPiW76ew_eA3A59rXX3UxQwwTCc-VC3XyVzCq3Oc1r4rTe7_ttC5R9fJvPHVAelJcqhax5ZyWt3XUdeuTYoLUwSCerU9-azEoAu-AV387BMkSDEveyYuywi0yQ9aUC7AGtSVuPkfXUjdJKvesTfaJgmXlt6l3dJs5cGEVWQAQEuyQSwNek1bQkfvkzUkr4k0Ci0Fbp-gq3dlDXtoMzHq7xc_yMtD8t2_v6p5ytW4NnZqdiknsbJuoqVL9S8ZRAnXazUEUdKD6lM-Z_kMRJ1gAoNk_fq0xB-EIX6l-Q-5QdBKf8jqXSK_rPFyliq2q-AYlDMMBoYpccyTP4ItYbi-DduDkummfFLcYT0K5ee5J6JsRaVr7Y12CyNNzyHtsq0FtWUrAX8Jq04MNe9hcxcvQmQgBolC5j8xsaWhjvct4lNofX5bBBS7ez00Ccq1OUOgeBIcIGmbS2rQTPRWZ6WmI0ZccPvUp7SbNaC8QwU-vvHX9ZASz2vjUq5p909TN1EuNiSxMhv8siBfo-u_fbZdhcgV9N1ItWRWc2Py4Io3yfQZJs847BuuqVeXYRe12AQWaJAoZwlbJ6PE7cgDgthrqB7TOWMO_jPD4d51NYSqF5nza8EOWOMkMKdNmw%3D)
Hi there,
The way we teach history shapes how the next generation sees America—and right now, that story is changing.
This past Wednesday, I took a closer look at how American history is presented in classrooms today. And what I found was striking. According to a Northwestern University Institute for Policy Research survey, 73% of Americans are dissatisfied with the way the subject is taught in public schools.
That stat tells you everything—parents across the political spectrum recognize that something is wrong.
As you know, these new curricula emphasize systemic challenges and injustices. **Students graduate without understanding the full story—the courage, sacrifice, and vision that built this nation. That's one reason the work of the Moving Picture Institute (MPI) matters so much to me. At MPI, we make movies that highlight the ideals of freedom, character, and service, and help bring these important stories to life for new audiences.**
And this matters more now than ever before. A generation is growing up without access to the stories and films that you and I had. We grew up with movies like _D-Day_ , _Davy Crocket_ , _The Alamo_ , _Top Gun_ —heck, just 20 years ago they made _The Patriot_.
But MPI is counteracting that by making a movie for families with children.

clean_body: Counteracting Classroom Propaganda Son of 1776 needs your support to reach millions of young Americans with the true story of America's founding. Hi there, The way we teach history shapes how the next generation sees America—and right now, that story is changing. This past Wednesday, I took a closer look at how American history is presented in classrooms today. And what I found was striking. According to a Northwestern University Institute for Policy Research survey, 73% of Americans are dissatisfied with the way the subject is taught in public schools. That stat tells you everything—parents across the political spectrum recognize that something is wrong. As you know, these new curricula emphasize systemic challenges and injustices. Students graduate without understanding the full story—the courage, sacrifice, and vision that built this nation. That's one reason the work of the Moving Picture Institute (MPI) matters so much to me. At MPI, we make movies that highlight the ideals of freedom, character, and service, and help bring these important stories to life for new audiences. And this matters more now than ever before. A generation is growing up without access to the stories and films that you and I had. We grew up with movies like D-Day , Davy Crocket , The Alamo , Top Gun —heck, just 20 years ago they made The Patriot. But MPI is counteracting that by making a movie for families with children. Son of 1776 is an animated film where a young patriot joins George Washington and experiences the American Revolution. Children and families will see the bravery and sacrifice that forged this great nation. This is a movie that WILL celebrate America's 250th birthday. | | ---|---|--- | | Sincerely, Joseph Corey Vice President of Philanthropic Investments The Moving Picture Institute | 375 Greenwich Street New York NY 10013

We are writing today to ask you to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin's campaign committee.

We are writing today to ask you to make a contribution to Elissa Slotkin's campaign committee.
You may be asking, Elissa just won her Senate race and the next election is only months away – why are you asking me to contribute again?
First, it goes without saying that Elissa Slotkin won Michigan – and so did Donald Trump.
One of the reasons that happened is because we did better than typical Democrats in the "redder" parts of the state. That is something that has happened consistently in Elissa's previous elections. She might not win them outright, but she "loses better."

But even in other parts of the country, Elissa is getting a lot of requests to join Democrats in tough races campaign trail. And given the importance of this election, she wants to do everything she can to help.
That takes resources. We're not asking for a huge contribution today, just whatever you feel is worth it to help Democrats hold statewide offices, our other Senate seat, and to flip the House.

While we await the results for some of the most competitive primaries of 2026, I wanted to take a moment to highlight a few of the headlines from this primary season that you helped make possible. **Each one gives me so much hope about the fight ahead against Donald Trump and his dirty fossil fuel agenda:** | **Deb Haaland, chasing history, wins Democratic New Mexico governor nod** **_— USA TODAY_**
---
**In New Mexico,** Deb Haaland won her Democratic primary for Governor. I've worked alongside Deb for years, and I can tell you firsthand — she is exactly the kind of leader our movement fights to put in office.
**State Rep. Chris Rabb wins Democratic primary for Philly congressional seat, a decisive win for the progressive left** **_— The Philadelphia Inquirer_**
---
**In Pennsylvania,** Rep. Chris Rabb went up against a crowded field in one of the most competitive congressional primaries in the country, and he won _decisively._ That's what happens when a climate champion has a grassroots movement at his back instead of a corporate checkbook.
**“Rep. Christian Menefee wins Democratic primary for 18th House District in Texas...”** **_— ABC NEWS_**
---
**In Texas,** the top oil-producing state in the country, our endorsed climate champion Christian Menefee won a hard-fought runoff to become the Democratic nominee for TX-18.
**What does the primary’s biggest legislative upset say about the state of Oregon politics?** **_— Oregon Public Broadcasting_**
---
**In Oregon,** Myrna Muñoz unseated an incumbent backed by the very corporate interests and fossil fuel companies poisoning our air, water, and communities.
_This was by far the most expensive legislative race in the state, and victory was far from guaranteed._ But Myrna proved what’s possible when unwavering organizing meets an unrelenting message centered on the people.
* * *
I know it can feel like there’s a shortage of hope in this world. But I hope you see the impact you’ve made as a supporter of my Climate PAC.
Every dollar you chipped in. Every email you opened. Every conversation you had with a friend or neighbor about why this fight matters. It all led here.

That's what happens when a climate champion has a grassroots movement at his back instead of a corporate checkbook. “Rep. What does the primary’s biggest legislative upset say about the state of Oregon politics? — Oregon Public Broadcasting In Oregon, Myrna Muñoz unseated an incumbent backed by the very corporate interests and fossil fuel companies poisoning our air, water, and communities. As voters hit the polls Tuesday to make their picks in this year’s primary races, a fresh lawsuit against California’s secretary of state is calling into question whether hundreds of thousands of unqualified voters were still eligible to head to the ballot box.Orange County Supervisor Don Wagner, the Republican candidate for secretary of state, joined the American Independent Party of California in suing incumbent Secretary of State Shirley Weber, alleging that 873,092 inactive voter registrations are still on the rolls.The complaint, filed through conservative voting watchdog organization Judicial Watch, claimed the Democrat Weber is in violation of federal law that requires most inactive voter registrations to be removed after two general federal elections.Instead, more than 800,000 registrations have remained inactive and on the rolls for at least three elections — with 151,202 on the rolls after at least four consecutive elections, the suit claims.The lawsuit also alleges that the state takes no effective action to require counties to fix the issue, citing admissions by California officials.A lawsuit alleges that 873,092 inactive voter registrations are still on the rolls.Currently, over 23 million Californians are registered to vote.Back in 2019, Judicial Watch had settled with the state of California and Los Angeles County to remove more than 1.2 million names from the voter rolls. Since then, the organization claimed 20 counties across the state have only removed 50 or fewer inactive voters, despite census data showing hundreds of thousands of residents leaving California.“Judicial Watch’s federal lawsuit confirms California has a dirty voting rolls crisis — with thousands of old names on the rolls going back at least 10 years,” Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton said in a statement. “Dirty voting rolls can mean dirty elections. And California and its counties must take immediate steps to clean the over 870,000 dirty names on the voting lists.”

subject: Donald Trump is handing the gun lobby another win

body:
We need to raise our voices right now.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3376%2E21716%2E4zidfD)
Every day, too many families in Delaware and across the country wake up to an empty seat at the table. This Gun Violence Awareness Day, I’m thinking of the lives stolen, the futures lost, and the far-too-familiar heartbreak so many families know.
For me, this fight is personal. I’ve stood with survivors. I’ve pleaded alongside advocates. And I’ve grieved with friends who lost loved ones in mass shootings — including at the Pulse Nightclub, which happened 10 years ago this month.
**I’ve seen the pain gun violence leaves behind. I’ve also seen what’s possible when we act.**
In the Delaware State Senate, I helped pass one of the most significant gun safety packages in our state’s history, banning assault weapons and strengthening background checks. Taking on the NRA wasn’t easy, but it was worth it.
**Today, in Congress, I’m fighting for the same kind of bold, commonsense solutions on a national scale, but I’m counting on your support to get it done.**
Because right now, at a moment when gun violence continues to devastate families, Donald Trump is working to hand the gun lobby another win. **Just recently, Trump’s Department of Justice directed the USPS to roll back a 100-year-old law, allowing guns to be sent through the mail.**
This is exactly why we have to raise our voices right now — to demand Congress strengthen gun safety laws and prevent more lives lost.
[**Will you add your name to my petition demanding Congress pass stronger gun safety laws that keep our communities safe?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/signup/em20260605-gun-safety-petition/?source=em20260605-3376&t=2&akid=3376%2E21716%2E4zidfD)

name: Sue Anderbois
subject: Ward 3 PVD News
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
body:
| |
---
Hello Friends & Neighbors,

We are in full summer mode in Ward 3! The summertime market is in full swing, gardens across the neighborhood are in bloom — and the weather has finally warmed up! I’m looking forward to bumping into you in all corners of the ward now that so many folks are out and about walking and enjoying our beautiful neighborhoods!

A big thank you to everyone who came out to our May Ward 3 meeting at the Mount Hope Community Center! We had a great conversation about the sale of the Rochambeau Fire Station, traffic calming on Hope Street, and much more.

As always, there’s a lot going on in Providence, so I’ll hop right into it!

|
| **Update On The Green Revolving Fund** Great news! The Green Revolving Fund that I sponsored passed and has been signed by Mayor Smiley!

The Green Revolving Fund allows us to invest the savings from our investments in energy efficiency and clean energy back into a revolving fund to help fund future projects. You might remember that two years ago, I wrote and then unanimously passed an ordinance requiring all municipal buildings to be carbon neutral by 2040. The City’s Sustainability Department has been hard at work on implementation!

With the attacks on clean energy at the federal level — and Governor McKee’s attempts to claw back support for clean energy in Rhode Island — Providence isn’t going to stand down. This Revolving Fund helps us basically reinvest our savings from greening our buildings (as well as any previous incentives we’ve received), and invest them in future projects — kind of making our own clean energy incentives!

**[You can hear more about it in this video I recorded!](https://sue4ri.com/l/kf1o2hd0Xqfm)** Investing in clean energy in Providence is not only helping the environment — it’s also saving us real money for our taxpayers AND creating good, local jobs! | | [ **WATCH HERE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/BqNgl8bU4pNO)
---

**Upcoming Events** **Ways & Means Committee:** The Ways & Means Committee (which has replaced the Finance Committee) continues to meet at least twice a week to review sections of the budget. **[You can see upcoming meetings and which departments are scheduled to present on the City’s Open Meetings Portal.](https://sue4ri.com/l/0I2WznSHnLwe)** When the second public hearing is scheduled, I will share that information here and also through my social media channels!
**City Council:** The City Council continues to meet as a full body on the 1st and 3rd Thursday of every month at 6 pm in the Council chambers!
**Miscellaneous:** Mount Hope Community Center Arts & Crafts Day at Billy Taylor Park — June 13th at 11 am!

---

**Miscellaneous Topics For You** There are quite a number of important topics before the Council and for our Ward right now – I wanted to just share a few!
**Ways & Means Committee:** Last month, the Council created a Special Committee on Ways and Means to handle the review of the budget and future finance committee matters. This replaces the Finance Committee for this term. As you know, I have been enthusiastically serving on the Finance and the Ways and Means Committee since my first week on Council.

Since I am not running for re-election, and it’s important to me to ensure continuity and strong financial oversight for the City, Councilwoman Davidson and I discussed it, and I have transitioned my seat on the Committee to Councilwoman Davidson so that she could have some time serving directly on this important committee before (hopefully!) being re-elected and returning to Council next term.

I will still enthusiastically participate, but I wanted to ensure that I was creating the space for our newest member to have this direct, hands-on experience. Councilwoman Davidson and I have a close relationship, and will continue to coordinate and work together on this and many other issues, and I appreciate her and that she was interested in digging in on this!
**MOHA Infrastructure:** I was so pleased to help shepherd a bond investment for new sidewalks and other infrastructure investments for Benefit Street late last year. Benefit Street spans 3 wards (1, 2, and 3), but is a historic treasure for the whole City and visiting tourists. I am so pleased that this past week, we kicked off implementation of this project with the Administration. The streets and sidewalks will be safer for pedestrians while maintaining their historic significance.
**Nathan Bishop Courts:** I am so pleased to share that the Nathan Bishop Courts will be reopening by the end of the month! I know folks have been waiting for a long time for this project to be completed, and I appreciate your patience! We listened to a great deal of community feedback (and the feedback of students and teachers!), and the new courts will be a mix of dedicated space for tennis, dedicated space for pickleball, basketball, and some open play space for the students.

I know that no one ‘got’ 100% of what they asked for – but I am grateful that we have such a well-loved community asset that so many folks advocated so passionately for! I will continue to work hard and advocate for increased access to high-quality open space! Keep an eye out — Councilwoman Davidson and I will be doing a ribbon cutting to celebrate these new courts at the end of June, and we’ll invite every one of you to join us in the celebration!

---

**Follow My Socials For Live Updates!** Between newsletters, I post frequent updates on more time-sensitive matters and general updates on what’s going on in council. You can follow below to make sure you don’t miss a thing! | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/9yigMYvPDSnB) | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/O1DwkLTNZLP8) | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/QZLn6PzV57Sa)
---|---|---

Thank you, thank you, thank you for the honor of serving you on the Providence City Council. I take this responsibility incredibly seriously, and I am grateful every day for the chance to serve you & our City.

Please reach out any time by replying to this email if there are issues of importance to you or ways I can be of service to you. Budget season is a busy season at City Hall, so thank you in advance for your patience if my email inbox gets a little flooded, and I take a day or two to respond — I do try to reply individually to every (non-form) email I receive!

With Gratitude,

Sue A
---
|
* * *
**** This communications is on behalf of Sue AnderBois' City Council work ****

Councilor Sue AnderBois represents Ward 3, which includes the Mount Hope, Hope Village (Summit), Collyer Park, and Blackstone neighborhoods. She currently serves as the Deputy Majority Whip and the Chair of the North Main Street Task Force and the Special Committee on Environment and Resiliency. She is also a member of the Committee on Finance, Committee on City Property, Special Committee on Health, Opportunity, Prosperity, and Education (HOPE), and is a member of the Board of Parks Commissioners.

Her career has been focused on public policy solutions for climate change, clean energy, and sustainable food systems.
---
| Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
---

166 5th St, PVD 02906

body:
Support from Louisiana’s forestry community adds to growing momentum in U.S. Senate race

| | |
---
| | | | [|

| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEJune 5, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**LETLOW EARNS ENDORSEMENT OF LOUISIANA LOGGERS ASSOCIATION** _Support from Louisiana’s forestry community adds to growing momentum in U.S. Senate race_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed conservative candidate for U.S. Senate, announced the endorsement of the Louisiana Loggers Association in her campaign for the United States Senate.
The Louisiana Loggers Association represents the hardworking men and women who power one of Louisiana’s most important industries and help support thousands of jobs across rural communities throughout the state.
_“Congresswoman Letlow understands the vital role the timber and logging industry plays in Louisiana’s economy and has consistently stood up for the hardworking men and women who keep this industry moving forward,”_**said Toni McAllister of the Louisiana Loggers Association.**_“She has been a strong advocate for rural Louisiana and has demonstrated a clear understanding of the challenges facing the logging industry, from rising operating costs to market uncertainty. Her commitment to supporting Louisiana’s timber and logging sector makes her a strong voice for our communities. We are proud to endorse her campaign for the United States Senate.”_
_**“I’m honored to have the support of the Louisiana Loggers Association and the hardworking men and women they represent,”**_**said Congresswoman Letlow.**_**“Forestry is a cornerstone of Louisiana’s economy and a vital part of many rural communities. I’ll continue fighting for policies that protect our loggers, strengthen Louisiana jobs, and ensure this important industry remains strong for generations to come.”**_
The endorsement comes as Letlow continues to deliver results for Louisiana’s forestry community. Earlier this year, the House passed her legislation to strengthen the Emergency Conservation Program, making it easier for farmers and forest landowners to recover from natural disasters.
Letlow, a native of Monroe, mother of two, educator, and sitting member of Congress, is running for the U.S. Senate as the Trump-endorsed conservative in the race. She has built her campaign around fighting for Louisiana families, supporting President Trump’s America First agenda, and delivering results for the people of Louisiana.
Learn more at [JuliaLetlow.com](https://us.list-manage.com/SPGed9jgwVe?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a).

Peter, I need to ask a favor of you. _**_This is personal_**._ I just heard something in a**__highly sensitive__** D.C. meeting that I cannot, in good conscience, accept. We can stop this. # [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=244%2E127862%2EB9Dxu-)
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260605_1_ak.Cg3ZIU&amount=5&refcode=em20260605-241&t=2&akid=244%2E127862%2EB9Dxu-)
As a former attorney general, I know exactly what it takes to do that job. Right now, Aaron Ford is doing incredible work as Nevada’s attorney general:
* He has held big drug companies accountable, winning $1.2 billion in settlements to fight the opioid crisis.
* He has protected tenants from predatory "junk fees" and fought to keep families in their homes.
* And he’s sued the Trump administration when they’ve targeted our fundamental rights — and won.

**But there’s a huge obstacle standing in the way of making even more progress for Nevadans: MAGA Governor Joe Lombardo.**
Lombardo consistently works against what Aaron is fighting for. He has vetoed critical bills to crack down on corporate landlords and lower the cost of housing.
**_Lombardo even said Nevadans should _“feel a little pain”_ from Donald Trump’s tariffs._**
Nevada families don't need any more pain. They need real leadership, and Lombardo isn’t cutting it.
**That’s why I am proud to support Aaron’s campaign for governor.** He is ready to take his record of results to the governor’s office, but the conservative machine is pouring everything they have into keeping Lombardo in power.
**[We have to show them that grassroots power is stronger than special interests. Will you chip in $5 — or whatever you can — today to help Aaron win this toss-up race?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260605_1_ak.Cg3ZIU&amount=5&refcode=em20260605-241&t=3&akid=244%2E127862%2EB9Dxu-)**

name: Team Collins
subject: Graham Platner is simply not working
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Collins for Senator
body:
CHIP IN RIGHT NOW!
| Fellow American,
There is a stark difference between a Maine work ethic and a Washington political stunt.
The Radical Left's poster boy, Graham Platner, has plenty of time to pose for magazine covers and sit for glowing interviews with the New York Times.
Why? Because he simply isn't working.
He claims to be a "working-class oyster farmer," but the reality is far different. For the past decade, Platner has not held a full-time job. He has been passively growing oysters and enjoying a leisurely life, all while Chuck Schumer and Elizabeth Warren prop him up as their handpicked candidate to flip Maine blue. Now, he is bending the truth in glossy photo shoots, trying to convince voters that he will work hard for our state.
Mainers know what real hard work looks like.
Compare Platner's record to Susan Collins'. Susan has never missed a roll call vote. She has never taken a sick day. She has never stopped fighting for Maine's interests in Washington.
