America did not begin as a perfect nation, but it did begin as a nation that openly recognized its dependence upon God. From the earliest colonial settlements to the drafting of the Declaration of Independence, faith played a central role in shaping the beliefs, values, and principles that would become the foundation of the United States. The men who built this nation were not all theologians, nor did they agree on every point of doctrine. However, they overwhelmingly understood that liberty, morality, and self-government could not survive without a strong moral foundation. Many Americans are told that faith should be separated entirely from public life.

## WWII Veteran, 100, Attends His First Prom
Eighty-two years after being drafted to serve in World War II and missing his high school prom, 100-year-old Ray Svejnoha finally got his dance. Students at [Metea Valley High School](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAQRk9jd7aGibFJQbFNumy7JcIwOLOLwcIoKLdfOVf46_c0o_f9eZqn5chp-2130mELpoZsErUzUq1UTOBy1qPk3VYB4HL-x3TkRsUg4DzAPIA03nL8mKn3OhAh3XrSYlEwq_sdZf_SiwVyt8Xe3UqChFoUoZLWBQThZuV61tc1mEEigMRpxHW1YlXTCl4KP8luAvJccxn_Zk71RSF-8pvK6PLeR_2q9Ti7268OHx0-WmvjlZBs5ZxSbpfV4WPL2Q8X-DrMw5sqFZuGq29QOHzIlgv2RfujcYx8zks3wbZbjt9X9ccbvTX-DwAA___P1H1f) in Aurora, Illinois, learned his story through a club that helps seniors with technology and decided to give him the prom he never had. They surprised him with a promposal featuring red, white, and blue balloons and a sign reading "[82 years late, but right on time](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkM1uhSAUhJ8Gd9wcDuDPgkWTxm56u-3SoBy9tCgGiDe-fWP7CN3OTCbzzed9uFsf_LZ82JXMvMxDmeOw0TMHKoXSMPuUy57iaosAmGL89rTHJ6UBAWsONQc9OOvDOajKmZkISVZkRNNC3XYd6uphCDsE56QWQmjbjbVWjZuaBqXqQLZz5c3VBjVoBNCobjiOVoytGsFp4ZRmCsj5EtPtK_qtPGgOZzwo3aa4VsE8Stkzky8Me4a9HaeL4PIY9m_3S373h98Whr0A4CfZxA8qlOzGbSm0ucxFLvwC5e1fIDPsc4npZLL3jslXISUKVWNTJeP2pw_B57phCpbV-vC7pPz7wsPgTwAAAP__U3WDZw)." Community sponsors chipped in with a haircut, manicure, tuxedo fitting, and a vintage trolley ride to the event, where students greeted him with cheers and welcomed him onto the dance floor. [Ray took the microphone](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnsTuiBQO2C4q_SZe_vRJhsyR7h40Fq1h5-1PyClePNKNvvm7-FijTfv8fNnTpnjyn4nc8W0ZmrD5RbXzUsgWWAGspP4RHObF6BcoKsAKMj4Hyy-s-uoSocOjRyXECO82zMv3DmTDYAdao5zlMg8ZR42iSXe28SoiL6cm928CCUQBG6YtaliCXSS8QjYzadBowEpd6-S608wNTfpUn1statj67B_PRuuFfp66duh5YjozvqFPX8yQST2SsYReBGffYxEcl3iwRWEgA8cJQmyg5CinnSSst--ricVLO1OzYabhvgfJnj_981NOp3wAAAP__HGt9Ow) to address the crowd. "_I cannot tell you how much I appreciate this, and I love you all_ ," he said.
## Pianist in the Crowd Saves Opening Night
When the keyboard player fell ill halfway through the opening night of _La La Land in Concert_ in Sydney, Oscar-winning composer Justin Hurwitz [asked the crowd of 2,500](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQRp8GOiMz12bZwkUauk2bEvlnDJMYG9mzu-Lto00e4Upf90lHR-fXY31YSpS3n_ZAE7e4cixrxndLyIx1jVQbn7UclkcpfSl_CM_yxrqChEnISUi9BkvpWlUfTEQE_OrRjLdZTvP9DrrfjYV7BAXWRa8lglca0QVtHUyzu6HqyXxocpIapNSgBnDOjm5WTgY9BqU7JTEQlzr8LpR5x5iu8sI6-HL0yezMZ-u-fnSwdLB44mt_us832GcHi30GwuxRHHg4rKLZFzbBO4pgL2FZtCtkvJooJ2bKm8i07SxKFMn-Xw6CsvAle6zcwdJXE843pURtunVKboel9E-Gv13xZeBvAAAA___Q7You) if anyone could sight-read. Sterling Nasa, a 21-year-old university student, raised his hand after a nudge from his friend, who told him, "_just do it, it'll be good dad lore_." Within minutes, Sterling was seated with the [full orchestra and jazz ensemble](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOnDAQRL8Gbj0yjQ3MwYfRJkgbZdgoiZQjMrg9ODEYNc5a_H20Sf5gpTqWSvXej_t4Nz747TGYlbR7uDG5OG6Uj0ApEY_O85F2jqtJlRBzjL887TETjyiwAdGAUKM1PpyjLK12REh1SbpqO9F01yuqctGdbJVTRFjXlXXYXVuF2JLsrJnqazuXXr-tiUYoFEKhvOA0mWrq5CSsqqxUhRRkfYp8-Rn9lhZy4YyvxJc5rmXQS0r7UdS3AvsC-5zzZeJobDZnjhzsW6vA3nDyc6AC-9tv62mbCe60TsTwKfrtgBeeFzoSG-gjw-fbvwwf4HmAp5fh6ePX7-A3-HbajU64uUQMX4hd5JUYehPCAc8hwH-WqmRt9-xD8EfTFlI8VuPD38fp3apfNf4JAAD__-KNkzA), playing a celeste he'd never touched before. When a technical solo arrived that he couldn't sight-read, he improvised it instead. Hurwitz later told Sterling he had worried there wouldn't be a synth solo if he couldn't get through the part. Instead, the crowd gave the unlikely substitute a standing ovation. "_I was a little bit tentative_ ," [Sterling said](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuu2zAQRL-G6iisV--CRRp1N21KgY-VtQ5FCtTagvP1gZNPuMCUg8Gc8-tr-bIcOd1_2p3Mel8XWfOS6DojiVBZVi6nHCXvVm4APuffTEe-qCwI2GvoNXRLsBzfS1sFsxIhNRWZ2zBCP04TdtVmLJKjyTrbBETnm973HmByAzU0tG1TsfmsQQ8dAnTY1uicvbmxdRC6W2g71QIFllzqR-YkG63xnV9Uap_3KppN5DhV80PhrHC-rquWjTSnQAelQEk-PYWzLXJqSkJFLKedkiicZSMrhXSwyZPC-UOvcD7fIdFbR_s_KejH8xROenuWi-WPts_AlDxpn5OnIvrFgbJ2OI0DjE29yR6rYsJxcYx89oNq4b5bjv9Oy7dtvwz-DQAA__-mD5iP). ## Flight Attendant Retires After 66 Years in the Sky

Students at in Aurora, Illinois, learned his story through a club that helps seniors with technology and decided to give him the prom he never had. They surprised him with a promposal featuring red, white, and blue balloons and a sign reading "." Community sponsors chipped in with a haircut, manicure, tuxedo fitting, and a vintage trolley ride to the event, where students greeted him with cheers and welcomed him onto the dance floor. to address the crowd. "I cannot tell you how much I appreciate this, and I love you all ," he said. Pianist in the Crowd Saves Opening Night When the keyboard player fell ill halfway through the opening night of La La Land in Concert in Sydney, Oscar-winning composer Justin Hurwitz if anyone could sight-read. Sterling Nasa, a 21-year-old university student, raised his hand after a nudge from his friend, who told him, "just do it, it'll be good dad lore." Within minutes, Sterling was seated with the , playing a celeste he'd never touched before. When a technical solo arrived that he couldn't sight-read, he improvised it instead. Hurwitz later told Sterling he had worried there wouldn't be a synth solo if he couldn't get through the part. Instead, the crowd gave the unlikely substitute a standing ovation. "I was a little bit tentative ," . "I do owe a lot of the experience to my friend Scarlett, who sort of put my hand up for me. But I did end up finding the confidence, and it was a very good decision." Flight Attendant Retires After 66 Years in the Sky Joan Prince Crandall took her last flight on May 30 after , retiring as the longest-serving flight attendant in aviation history. The Delta Air Lines crew member, now in her 80s, started as a stewardess at Pacific Airlines in 1959, flying propeller planes that held as few as 24 passengers. "That has been my career—from stewardess to flight attendant ," said Joan, who was in January after surpassing the previous record of 64 years. Her career spanned six airlines through decades of mergers, landing her at Delta in 2008. Before retiring, Joan met Alise Broussard, a newly graduated Delta flight attendant just starting her career. Those awarded the distinction have demonstrated that they will support stronger gun laws and advocate for safer communities if elected into office." — Moms Demand Action Gun Sense website In the wake of each devastating death by gun violence, we must remember that we can best honor those lives lost and the families they leave behind by working to end this epidemic. It is within our power to champion gun safety legislation. It is in your power to vote. Together, we can take a stand against gun violence. body:
First, thanks for opening this email. I mean that — it helps out more than you might realize.
#

Hey everybody, it’s Mark.
I’ve got two things for you today.
First, thanks for opening this email. I mean that — it helps out more than you might realize.
And second, I’m going to ask you to click the link below and fill out the form it takes you to. I’d like to know what you, personally, think is the most important challenge facing our country right now.
Here’s that link:
[**https://act.markkelly.com/go/Survey**](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/survey_em_june26/?source=em260605-1-M2&refcode2=6494.6688874.0lDczE&akid=6494%2E6688874%2E0lDczE)
The reason I’m asking you to do this isn’t all that complicated. When I’m in the Senate I get to talk to people all the time, hear their stories, and learn what’s important to them. The same goes for when I’m traveling, meeting people at home in Arizona or anywhere else around the country.
But with emails like this, it’s not often I get to hear directly from you. This is an opportunity for me to get some active feedback, and I’d like to take advantage of it now while we still have about five months until the election.
That’s it, really. So, how about it?
[**Use this link and take a minute to let me know what you think the most important challenge ahead of us is. It’d be great to hear from you.**](https://act.markkelly.com/signup/survey_em_june26/?source=em260605-1-M2&refcode2=6494.6688874.0lDczE&akid=6494%2E6688874%2E0lDczE)
Thanks in advance,
Mark

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you want to, you can [ unsubscribe here](https://act.markkelly.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=1&akid=6494%2E6688874%2E0lDczE).

name: LeftNet
subject: It doesn’t have to be this way
body:
This month is Gun Violence Awareness Month.
#
_Content Warning: This email contains mention of gun violence and mass shootings. If that’s too heavy for you right now, feel free to skip the rest of this email and wherever you are, please take care of yourself._
June marks Gun Violence Awareness Month — but in the U.S., _every month and every day_ leaves another family and community devastated.
In the first 155 days of this year, there have already been **169 mass shootings.**
[****](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260605.sU7CbC&refcode=em20260605-1651&amount=5&t=1&akid=1651%2E2118727%2EAAL1m3)
For every shooting, we’ve grown accustomed to what has become a repetitive process that plays out in cities and towns across the country.
**But we don’t have to live like this.**
Gun violence isn’t inevitable — **it’s a policy failure.** And we know what the solutions are:
✅ Universal background checks
✅ Red flag laws
✅ Community-based violence intervention programs
✅ Banning assault weapons
✅ Holding the gun lobby and industry accountable
None of these policies are radical. In fact, common-sense gun regulations are popular across the U.S. — even among Republicans.
It’s about damn time our elected leaders heed the call for action and offer real solutions, not just empty thoughts and prayers.
This month, we’re supporting the grassroots organizations who are on the front lines of America’s gun violence epidemic — and they could use your help.**
**
A future free of gun violence isn’t out of reach. With real action, we can save lives _and_ protect our communities. **[Please pitch in a split contribution of $5 or anything you can spare today to support the grassroots groups who are trying to make this future a reality.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260605.sU7CbC&refcode=em20260605-1651&amount=5&t=2&akid=1651%2E2118727%2EAAL1m3)**
_Your contribution will be split between the following organizations: Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund, Giffords, and March For Our Lives Action Fund._
**[Pitch In ➡️](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260605.sU7CbC&refcode=em20260605-1651&amount=5&t=3&akid=1651%2E2118727%2EAAL1m3)**
In solidarity,
LeftNet

You may have seen the email we sent you yesterday about our new voter registration program.
I wanted to follow up personally, because this work is close to my heart.
I've been organizing in Texas for years. I've watched voters get turned away, get confused, give up — not because they didn't want to vote, but because nobody was there to help them navigate a system that was designed to be confusing.
This week, our partners mailed voter registration forms to 150,000 Texans who have recently moved — 50,000 from out of state, 100,000 from within Texas.
But the mailer is only the beginning.
My job — our job — is to make sure every single one of those voters actually gets registered. That means texts. Phone calls. Follow-ups. Staying with them all the way to November.
This is behind-the-scenes work. It doesn't often make headlines. But it is the real work that wins elections.
These are exactly the voters who could decide the outcome of James Talarico vs. the corrupt Ken Paxton. We cannot leave them on the table. Plus we have opportunities to make unexpected friends along the way...
**It’s going to cost Powered by People at least $66,000 to cover the texts, calls, and contact data needed to reach all of these Texans.**

---
Friend,
This is going to be a long email. At the end, [_**I’m going to ask you to make a ****donation to my campaign for governor of Colorado.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132788644/625682907/-1487442751?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1445-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZmEzNmQxOC0xZTYxLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FxMgPdmv9Jv0lkqTH0QPvFn14YZtH0KD6RsBm1Yhi7o=)** ** But before I do, I want to share a photo that reminds me why I'm running in the first place:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132788645/625682908/-1487442751?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1445-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZmEzNmQxOC0xZTYxLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FxMgPdmv9Jv0lkqTH0QPvFn14YZtH0KD6RsBm1Yhi7o=)
Running for governor wasn't part of the plan when Susan and I moved to Colorado in 1997 as newlyweds. It was just the perfect place for us to build our new life together.
We packed our things into a U-Haul hitched to her station wagon and set out on our very own American Dream. Because back then, it was within our reach.
**It's unacceptable to me that 30 years later, young folks have lost all hope of joining the middle class, buying a starter home and raising a family in our state** – the way we could at their age.
Throughout my career as a public servant, Coloradans have put their trust in me to fight for them in the U.S. Senate. I felt that responsibility deeply and still do.
I also knew that the best way to protect people struggling through a new Gilded Age – made worse by Trump's corruption and the corporate greed our governor has failed to rein in – was to start here in our state.
That's why I couldn't sit out this race. And I'm confident we can win.
Since launching my campaign, thousands have joined our movement to make Colorado the best place to live, work and raise a family. I’m so grateful to count you among them.
But my primary opponent is making massive ad buys to crowd our vision off the airwaves. A super PAC funded by private equity and Big Oil and Gas bigwigs is also broadcasting lies about me to help him knock us out of the race.
**So if I'm going to get to work on Day One bringing the American Dream back within reach in Colorado as our next governor, I need your help to keep up our momentum and secure the Democratic nomination**.
_[**If you're able to give today, please donate $5, or any amount you can toward our $70,000 goal ahead of our public filing deadline on Wednesday. Since I'm in this fight to solve the affordability crisis squeezing Colorado families and build opportunity for the next generation, this campaign isn't funded by corporate PACs – so every donation makes a difference.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132788646/625682909/-1487442751?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1445-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZmEzNmQxOC0xZTYxLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FxMgPdmv9Jv0lkqTH0QPvFn14YZtH0KD6RsBm1Yhi7o=)_

I didn't grow up with connections. I didn't have a family name that opened doors or a network that handed me opportunities. What I had was the belief that if you worked hard enough, the system would eventually work for you too.
It took years of real life to understand the harder truth: **the system wasn 't built for people like me and you.** It was built for people who already had everything and needed just a little more.

## Elon's Trillion-dollar rocket ride
SpaceX IPO makes Musk the first Trillionaire
SpaceX is hitting the Nasdaq next week. **[Elon Musk's ownership stake there alone is worth over $866 billion.](https://substack.com/redirect/4b68f788-ea2d-4b73-a6f5-311e7ab05047?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Stack that on his $350 billion plus in Tesla and the man crosses the one trillion dollar net worth line. First in history.
After Tesla's public debut 16 years ago, this is the next chapter. SpaceX pulled in $18.67 billion in revenue last year. Haters will scream bubble, but they said the same about Tesla. Starlink, space dominance, Mars ambitions - the future is priced in. Musk retains over 82% voting control. One year lock-up, then the sky's the limit.
Shareholders win huge. Early SpaceX investors get liquid. The entire Musk ecosystem benefits. Who loses? The perpetual doubters and shorts getting torched again. This is unapologetic capitalism rewarding audacious execution. Musk's wealth isn't a problem; it's proof the system works when a maniac builds empires.
The dip or any volatility post-IPO? Buy it. We're watching the creation of the ultimate wealth machine. Get on board or get left behind.

# Microsoft and OpenAI's relationship crumbles as MS goes rogue
The **[Microsoft-OpenAI romance is dead. Now they're frienemies at best.](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce4fcca-7bb5-4d66-950f-acbc3d6ae244?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce4fcca-7bb5-4d66-950f-acbc3d6ae244?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)On Tuesday Microsoft unveiled MAI-Thinking-1, its own midsize AI model designed for high-efficiency tasks. They claim it matches Anthropic's Claude on coding benchmarks. This move screams one thing: Microsoft is done being overly reliant on OpenAI for its Copilot products.
They've poured $13 billion into the startup since 2019 but OpenAI's constant demands for more compute power strained things. Microsoft lost exclusive cloud provider status in January 2025 and first refusal rights in October. The April agreement rewrite killed exclusive IP access and revenue sharing payments from Microsoft.
Brilliant strategy by Microsoft. They're shifting to a model-agnostic approach where users pick the best tool, whether OpenAI, Anthropic, or their own. OpenAI plans its IPO later this year while battling Anthropic.
Who wins? Microsoft and its shareholders. Less risk, developing internal capabilities, better control over costs and tech. Who loses? OpenAI as their biggest partner flexes independence.
What's next? Expect more big tech building proprietary AI to reduce dependency. Partnerships are temporary in this cutthroat game. Microsoft is protecting its empire ruthlessly. That's how you stay on top. Diversify or die. This AI war is just heating up and only the smart money survives.

# **Uber 's HR massacre
23% of "People and Places"" division executed for efficiency **
Uber just carved out **[23% of its People and Places team.](https://substack.com/redirect/0edd827f-98ee-40a3-8d9d-3d60f69bfe4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** HR, recruiters, facilities managers, culture czars - all getting the chop. Mostly senior roles. The whole thing is still less than 1% of their 34,000 global workforce, but the symbolism is loud and clear.
Jill Hazelbaker, freshly promoted to president and chief corporate affairs officer, is running point. She called the division too complex and fragmented, with overlapping responsibilities and teams disconnected from the business. Her mission: build a more connected, modern, operationally excellent organization. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi backed her completely, saying changes maximize effectiveness and unlock potential.
Not blaming AI here, they insist. Good, because they're already using it heavily in engineering. Bookings grew 25% last quarter. Robotaxi bets are on. Hiring continues in key areas. HR folks lose their remote work deal - three days in the office now.
Shareholders win. Costs drop, bureaucracy shrinks, profits expand. The overhead lifers lose hard. This small dip in the stock is noise. Buy opportunity. Uber is shedding dead weight to run faster. Expect more of this disciplined approach. In this game, only the ruthless survive and thrive. That's the play.

# **Labor market still punching hard
122K jobs added beats expectations**
ADP just dropped a bomb: **[private payrolls jumped 122,000 in May,](https://substack.com/redirect/9a454f96-3ef5-4ee8-8e0b-84e66936504d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** crushing the 110k estimate and up from April's revised 105k. Broad-based too - not just healthcare this time. Education and health led, but trade, transportation, construction, even leisure all chipped in. Small businesses leading the charge.
This screams resilient economy guys. Labor market's got legs heading into summer. Pay growth steady at 4.4% for stayers, 6.5% for job hoppers. Good for workers, great for consumer spending, but the Fed's gonna be watching this like hawks before their June meeting. Rates staying put is the base case.
Who wins? Companies in a strong hiring environment keep growing. Stock market futures mixed but this supports the soft-landing narrative. Losers? Anyone betting on imminent recession or big rate cuts - those dreams just got delayed.
Next? Friday's official nonfarm payrolls will confirm. If this momentum holds, we're looking at a Goldilocks scenario: growth without overheating. But don't get complacent. Strong jobs can keep rates higher for longer, which punishes the debt-laden and rewards cash flow kings. Play the strength.

# **Sellers folding like cheap suits in a cooling housing market**
Sellers are **[yanking homes off the market faster](https://substack.com/redirect/c5c916bd-d2d8-479e-bd79-874d5dfbd444?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** than they've done since the damn pandemic shut everything down in 2020. Redfin says 5.8% of listings got delisted in April - up 3.8% from March. Atlanta's leading the charge with one in ten homes pulled. Why? Higher mortgage rates, gas prices through the roof, and buyers finally growing a pair and lowballing offers. Sellers aren't getting the fat prices they dreamed of anymore.
This is the spring selling season, for chrissakes, and these clowns are tapping out. What it really means is the housing party is over. Buyers are in the driver's seat for the first time in years. Smart money wins here - negotiate hard, inspect everything, and don't overpay. Losers? The delusional sellers who think their McMansion is still worth 2022 bubble prices. They're about to get crushed or sit on empty houses.
Next move? More inventory piling up as spring ends. Prices will flatten or dip in rate-sensitive markets. This is your cue to hunt for deals before the next wave of motivated sellers floods in. Real estate investors who stay disciplined are gonna eat. The weak hands? They're done.

# **SPACE X BLASTS OFF**
# **Musk nails $135 Fixed IPO Price at $1.75 Trillion valuation**
Elon Musk's **[SpaceX is targeting a fixed $135 per share for its IPO roadshow at a staggering $1.75 trillion valuation.](https://substack.com/redirect/b99380ea-c3ba-4553-878c-d399935fe0f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** That's right - no games, no price range dance. They're set to raise $75 billion selling 555.6 million shares and list on Nasdaq June 12 as SPCX. This will be the largest IPO ever, and it'll make SpaceX the seventh largest US company, surpassing Tesla.
What does it really mean? Musk is flexing. With Starlink generating serious revenue despite losses from R&D, and Starship on the horizon, this is fuel for the empire. Talk of merging with Tesla is the cherry on top - imagine that combined monster.
Winners? Musk, whose net worth skyrockets further. Early investors and employees cashing in huge. Smart capital chasing the space and AI future.
Losers? Competitors getting obliterated. Shorts about to get torched. Anyone too timid to play in the big leagues.
Next move? The roadshow will be a madhouse. Demand will be insane. Post-IPO, expect volatility but upward trajectory as they deploy that cash hoard. This is capitalism at its finest. Bold bets, massive rewards. Get positioned or watch from the sidelines while the rocket launches.

They've poured $13 billion into the startup since 2019 but OpenAI's constant demands for more compute power strained things. Microsoft lost exclusive cloud provider status in January 2025 and first refusal rights in October. The April agreement rewrite killed exclusive IP access and revenue sharing payments from Microsoft. Uber 's HR massacre 23% of "People and Places"" division executed for efficiency Uber just carved out HR, recruiters, facilities managers, culture czars - all getting the chop. Mostly senior roles. For data integrity purposes, please do not complete this survey if your email address is not dpwillis67@gmail.com .
435 has been the number of representatives in the U.S. House of Representatives since the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929. Even as our country has grown in population from 123 million back then to 343 million now, the number of people in Congress has not changed. You're just farther from your Congressional representative in the House than ever before (along with more than 761,000 others).
Some in the country recommend tying the size of a Congressional district to the smallest state by population, which is currently Wyoming. I f this were the case, the House would jump from 435 members to 575 , while your local Congressperson would represent only roughly 585,000 people -- roughly 200,000 fewer than today.

body:
Peter,

This weekend, I'm getting on a plane. Or actually, many planes.

Minnesota. Iowa. Colorado. Three states... One weekend.

First, I'm heading to Minnesota to keynote the Minnesota DFL Humphrey-Mondale dinner and campaign with Amy Klobuchar, who is running one of the most important governor's races in the country. And then I'm in Denver to keynote the Colorado Democratic Party’s Obama Gala, because we’ve got to keep Colorado in Democratic hands. Then I'm off to Des Moines to stand with Rob Sand, a Democrat who can flip Iowa's governorship blue for the first time in 15 years.

As chair of the Democratic Governors Association, this is my job, and I love doing it. Because I know something that a lot of people in D.C. have forgotten: governors deliver.

We fix roads. We fund public schools. We protect healthcare. We stand up for our people against an out-of-control federal government. Governors are where the rubber meets the road.

And right now, Democrats have a real shot at building a firewall of governors across this country, from Minnesota to Iowa to Colorado and beyond, but only if we have the resources to compete.

That's where you come in.

Peter,
We have a plan to knock on tens of thousands of doors. All in one weekend.
How? That’s where you come in.
If you’ve got time [this Monday night](https://act.francescahong.com/go/13741?t=1&akid=2883%2E105371%2E2TziEB) from 5-6 p.m., join us for an organizing call. We’ll help you get involved, whether that means joining your neighborhood volunteer team, persuading voters, or making some calls of your own.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Happy Pride Month, Peter!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
This month and every month, I stand with the LGBTQIA+ community.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260605-6320-footer&t=1&akid=6320%2E420207%2EPTyx2y)
Happy Pride Month, Peter! 🏳️🌈
I get so excited to march in the Seattle Pride Parade every June! I look forward to it all year 🏳️🌈 Being in the middle of the crowd surrounded by so much joy and love feeds my soul.
It’s moments like these that keep me going. That joy reminds me of what's possible when people come together, and gives me the motivation to keep fighting for our communities in Congress and at home.
Pride Month is a celebration, as it should be! And we celebrate loudly, joyfully, and without apology.
But it’s also a commitment. A commitment to continue showing up for each other and fighting for a world where everyone can live freely, love openly, and be who they are without shame or fear.
I don’t want to sugarcoat how difficult this past year has been. The Trump Administration is doing everything in its power to roll back the rights and freedoms for LGBTQIA+ Americans we fought for.
They’ve targeted trans kids in schools, stripped health care protections, punished providers for offering gender-affirming care, and used the full force of the federal government to threaten the safety and dignity of people who simply want to live their lives.
It’s cruelty, plain and simple. And I refuse to accept it.
To the LGBTQIA+ community: I see you. I hear you. I celebrate you. And I will never, not for a single moment, stop fighting for your right to live fully and freely as exactly who you are.
[**If you’re able, will you pitch in $3 to help keep me in Congress fighting for the LGBTQIA+ community?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260605.wjGwH3&refcode=em20260605-6320&amount=3&t=2&akid=6320%2E420207%2EPTyx2y)

With love and solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

name: David Hogg
subject: We’re investing in our future
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Legislatures have a major impact on our lives.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260605-1&t=1&akid=3566%2E587540%2EvMKtL4)
Peter,
We talk a lot about Congress, but state legislatures are a HUGE focus for us.
State legislatures are so important. They’re where district lines get drawn. They’re where abortion bans get blocked or passed, where Medicaid gets expanded or gutted, where working families either get a seat at the table or get left out entirely while corporations write the rules. Legislatures have a major impact on our lives.
And now, after SCOTUS gutted the Voting Rights Act, building power in state legislatures is even more important. More than 200 districts across the South are VRA districts — meaning we could get locked out of the South for a generation.
**But we aren’t giving up. We’re fighting back by electing bold young leaders to our state legislatures who will fight to make districts fair and representative.**
And that’s exactly why Leaders We Deserve is supporting a slate of strong legislative candidates, including three of our most recent endorsements:**Leila Staton** in Iowa, **Cat Clayton** in Missouri, and **Dinah Escarment** in Florida.
**[With your support, we can elect these leaders and many more to our state legislatures in November. Can you invest in that future with $5 now?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260605_1_state.nCJVAR&refcode=em20260605-3566&amount=5&t=2&akid=3566%2E587540%2EvMKtL4)**

David Hogg

body:
Check out these Independent candidates across the country...

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
The independent wave is building. This week, six key states held primaries that demonstrated, across the board, a growing tide of voters wanting more choice in their representatives. **Tuesday's Independent Candidates** Forward has been fighting the conventional wisdom in American politics: “If you want to win, you have to pick a team.” Well, voters are done with being handed two choices that no longer work for them. We are increasingly seeing candidates respond to that frustration by doing something the system has deliberately made difficult – running without a party label. This cycle, independent candidates are qualifying for November ballots from Montana to South Dakota, to Iowa, and more. They come from different backgrounds, different ideologies, and different regions. What they share is a conviction that the people of their districts deserve a representative who answers to them, not a party. Even more - in CA-06, the Democrats gerrymandered mid-cycle to try and gain more seats in Washington. Instead, voters are clear that they’ve had enough and an Independent is poised to win the top two primary. **California** California's uses a nonpartisan Top Two primary system which allows every candidate — Democrat, Republican, independent — appears on the same ballot. The top two finishers, regardless of party, advance to November. **Under this system, there is no "spoiler."** Top Two is one of the many reforms that Forward fights for nation-wide because they make our democracy better than it is today. California's June 2 primary was a strong test for independents (especially in a state with 30% “no party preference” voter registration). Under a partisan primary system, independent candidates have to wait until November. California's Top Two system is different. It is, as Forward has long argued, what every state's system should be: a fair fight, on one ballot, where voters choose who moves forward. Here's how our candidates fared.
* * *
| **Rep. Kevin Kiley** **California — CA-06** | Rep. Kevin Kiley did something remarkable this spring: he walked away from the Republican Party, choosing principle over party. After California's Proposition 50 redrew his district into solidly Democratic territory, Kiley could have retired, switched parties, or found a safe Republican-leaning seat. Instead, he filed as "No Party Preference," took the gerrymandering issue head-on, and made his case directly to voters.
---|---
With 53% of the district reporting Tuesday night, Kiley is **leading all candidates** in the Top Two primary with 26.8% of the vote. Final results are expected early next week. These results are showing Kiley advancing to the November general election, making him the first sitting independent member of the House of Representatives to survive a primary in 2026.
* * *
**Chris Demers** **California — CA-18** | Chris Demers entered the race as a No Party Preference candidate in a field that included both a major-party incumbent and challengers. Like many of our candidates, he isn't a career politician. He embodies Forward’s values by wanting to provide something better for his community.
---|---
With 54.8% of the district reporting, the race has been called for Rep. Zoe Lofgren and Republican Shane Lewis. Demers did not advance to November. But CA-18 is among the deepest Democratic districts in California – a seat that has never been seriously contested since Lofgren first won it. The fact that Chris Demers stood up, refused PAC money, and made the case for independent representation in one of the hardest possible environments is a step we are proud to see happen. Every independent candidate that runs in a district like this makes the next one easier. We're thankful for Chris Demers, and we hope he stays in the fight.
* * *
**Karen Leigh Matthews** **California — CA-23** | Dr. Karen Leigh Matthews is a Navy veteran, physician, radiologist, and small business owner who spent more than 20 years serving in the military. She ran for Congress as an independent because she was tired of being "caught between a party that wants government to fail and a party that wants government to do everything." That thinking, along with her resume, is something rare.
---|---
In CA-23, Karen outraised every Democratic challenger in the field. With Democratic support solidifying in the final days, the math narrowed her path to November and she fell short of advancing. With 61.3% of the district reporting, the race was called for incumbent Rep. Jay Obernolte (R). We are proud of Dr. Matthews and deeply grateful for her campaign. She showed what an independent candidate can look like when they're built for the job, not the party. Her district missed out on an exceptional public servant. We hope she runs again.
Before an independent candidate can even compete, they have to fight just to get their name on the ballot. Here's how Forward candidates made that happen in this cycle.
---
**Iowa**
**Michael Bridgford** **Iowa — IA-01** | **Michael Bridgford** is running in a district where roughly one-third of voters aren't registered with either major party. He officially filed his nomination petitions on June 1st, the day before the primary. He expects to pass the mark handily and qualify on to the ballot for November, we just need to wait for the Secretary of State to make it official.
---|---
**_The general election matchup:_**_Incumbent Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R) won her primary with 71.6% of the vote, while Christina Bohannon (D) won her primary with 81.5%. This will mark the third consecutive election in which these two candidates will face each other in the general. Iowa's 1st District voters know both options. Bridgford offers a third — one that doesn't arrive with three cycles of partisan theatrics._
* * *
**Dave Bushaw** **Iowa — IA-02** | **Dave Bushaw** is going to qualify for November’s ballot even though Iowa's legislature "moved the goalposts in the middle of the night," according to Dave, by raising the signature threshold mid-cycle. His campaign knocked on more than 7,000 doors and found that 88% of the people they spoke with wanted to sign. On June 2nd, Bushaw officially filed his nomination petitions. His campaign achieved 200% of the required signatures in every single county in IA-02.
---|---
We are continuing to monitor official approval, as signature challenges can be filed through next week, but Dave should sail through to November. **_The general election matchup:_**_Democrat Lindsay James, Dubuque state representative and Presbyterian minister, won with just under 60%, and will face Trump-backed Republican Joe Mitchell, who won with 61.5%. Notably, Democratic primary turnout in IA-02 outpaced Republican turnout: roughly 47,900 Democratic votes to roughly 39,700 Republican votes. Cook Political Report rates the seat Likely Republican, R+4 PVI, but calls it "increasingly competitive."_
* * *
**Montana**
**Seth Bodnar** **Montana** | **Seth Bodnar** needed 13,327 verified signatures from registered voters statewide to qualify for the November general election ballot as an independent in Montana. He didn't just meet the mark; he submitted nearly 30,000 signatures from 52 of Montana's 56 counties, collecting nearly twice the required threshold through a volunteer-driven grassroots petition effort. His campaign has also outraised every Democrat and Republican in the race, demonstrating that independent candidacy paired with serious organization is no longer a longshot strategy.
---|---
Bodnar officially filed his signatures in late May. As of May 29th, counties have accepted enough verified signatures to put Bodnar on the ballot. **_The general election matchup:_**_Kurt Alme (R) won his primary with 76.2% of the vote, while Alani Bankhead (D) won her primary with 43.8% of the vote._
* * *
**South Dakota**
**Brian Bengs** **South Dakota — U.S. Senate** | **Brian Bengs** is running for U.S. Senate in South Dakota with a grassroots campaign built on small-dollar donors. To qualify for the ballot as an independent in South Dakota, Bengs needed 3,502 valid signatures. He submitted more than 4,500 — and his petition was certified by the Secretary of State with a 93.85% validity rate, the highest of any statewide candidate in South Dakota this election season. That's better than both the Republican and Democratic candidates. The campaign called it "a testament to the strength of this movement." We agree.
---|---
He submitted his signatures in April and is officially on the November 3rd general election ballot, certified by the South Dakota Secretary of State. **_The general election matchup:_**_Incumbent Mike Rounds (R) won his primary with 75.8% of the vote, while Julian Beaudion (D) advanced unchallenged._
* * *
These aren't isolated data points. They are a trajectory. The independent political infrastructure – from the fundraising networks to the organizing capacity to the legal teams who know how to fight ballot challenges – is being built right now by the candidates and movements that keep showing up. Every campaign that plants a flag makes the next one possible.
---
**Forward Progress**
It would be easy to look at Tuesday's results and just count votes. However, the snapshot is bigger than any individual race. It is about a country that is waking up to the fact that the two-party system is not delivering for the people it's supposed to serve.
We don't just believe America can do better, we are actively building the infrastructure, recruiting the candidates, and making the case that voters deserve more than two choices handed to them by institutions that have long since stopped listening. Iowa, South Dakota, Montana, California, Washington, Minnesota, Maine, Tennessee, Rhode Island, and Nebraska are all seeing independent candidates qualify for ballots and create excitement. The movement is growing.
November is five months away. The work continues. And so does our question, _How can we build a just and fair government that truly represents Americans?_
One primary at a time. One candidate at a time. One voter at a time.

When the warning lights flash, you do not freeze. You rely on your discipline, face the threat head-on, and get the job done.
Well, Peter, the warning lights for our conservative majority are flashing red right now.
As a former Navy pilot who flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters, I know what it means to operate under intense pressure.
You sit in a loud, tight, shaking cabin for hours on end, flying over waters where there is no good place to land in case of an emergency.
Right now, the emergency is right here at home, and the stakes could not be higher.
The Democrats and their radical Left-wing Super PACs are dumping millions of dollars into Virginia to destroy my campaign.
In 2022, I flipped this district red in a tight, must-win race. The Democrats have not forgotten that, and they have not forgiven me for it. They are out for revenge!
They have vandalized my campaign office, destroyed my yard signs, and spent millions spreading vicious lies about me on television.
They know my seat is the key to the GOP majority. If we lose Virginia's 2nd District, Hakeem Jeffries becomes Speaker and the radical Left takes total control of Congress.
I am not a career politician. I am a mom, a Nurse Practitioner, and a former Navy pilot who stepped up to serve because I was tired of watching division and extreme rhetoric ruin our country. I know how to accomplish the mission, but I cannot fight off the Left's millions alone.
I need your help to hold the line, fight back against their smears, and keep our conservative majority intact.

You rely on your discipline, face the threat head-on, and get the job done. Well, Peter, the warning lights for our conservative majority are flashing red right now. As a former Navy pilot who flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters, I know what it means to operate under intense pressure. You sit in a loud, tight, shaking cabin for hours on end, flying over waters where there is no good place to land in case of an emergency. Right now, the emergency is right here at home, and the stakes could not be higher. The Democrats and their radical Left-wing Super PACs are dumping millions of dollars into Virginia to destroy my campaign. In 2022, I flipped this district red in a tight, must-win race. The Democrats have not forgotten that, and they have not forgiven me for it. They are out for revenge! They have vandalized my campaign office, destroyed my yard signs, and spent millions spreading vicious lies about me on television. They know my seat is the key to the GOP majority. If we lose Virginia's 2nd District, Hakeem Jeffries becomes Speaker and the radical Left takes total control of Congress. I am not a career politician. I am a mom, a Nurse Practitioner, and a former Navy pilot who stepped up to serve because I was tired of watching division and extreme rhetoric ruin our country. I know how to accomplish the mission, but I cannot fight off the Left's millions alone. I need your help to hold the line, fight back against their smears, and keep our conservative majority intact. | | | | | I appreciate you reading this all the way through. Your support means more to me than you will ever know! Thank you in advance, Jen I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you. Because of your support, I can keep fighting to make our country stronger. body:
Pictures attached
# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4895%2E898137%2E2BzDi5)
Hey ,
If you ask conventional political consultants how to win a U.S. Senate race, they’ll give you a very specific playbook. They’ll tell you to look at a spreadsheet, stick with the status quo, and don’t worry about the deep red districts.
They’ll tell you to skip the places that voted for Trump by 25 points. They’ll tell you it’s a waste of time.
**Well, we’ve never been big on traditional political playbooks.** We launched our _McMorrow On Tap_ tour because we believe you can’t say you want to represent a state if you only show up in the places where it’s comfortable. We promised we’d show up everywhere with open invitations to grab a drink and talk like neighbors.
[](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/6574?t=2&akid=4895%2E898137%2E2BzDi5)
We just stopped by Short’s Brewing out in Elk Rapids, and we wanted to send you a quick photo dump from the road because the energy blew us away. Look at this crowd:
[](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/6574?t=3&akid=4895%2E898137%2E2BzDi5)
It turns out that when you skip the highly rehearsed talking points and just show up ready to listen, people welcome you with open arms. Parents, neighbors, young people, folks who haven’t felt seen by a campaign in years — they’re all looking for a place where they feel welcome.
[](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/6574?t=4&akid=4895%2E898137%2E2BzDi5)
We’re proving that we can build a better tomorrow, but only if we’re brave enough to show up everywhere and talk to _everyone_.
But driving across the entire state — and keeping the gas tank full, the team organized, and our message on the airwaves everywhere — takes a lot of grassroots support. We don’t rely on shady corporate PACs, we rely on people like you.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. The U.S. Coast Guard will officially establish its new training center at Birmingham-Southern College later this week, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., announced Tuesday during a budget hearing with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

Britt, who chairs the Homeland Security appropriations subcommittee, said she will be on the 192-acre campus on Friday with Admiral Kevin Lunday to mark the milestone.

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-AL, has directly secured $2.063 million for the City of Foley through the Fiscal Year 2026 Homeland Security Appropriations Act to help strengthen the city’s infrastructure and improve storm resiliency during major tropical weather events.

The funding, secured by Britt in her role as chair of the Subcommittee on Homeland Security Appropriations, will support a project to relocate vulnerable overhead utilities underground in downtown Foley, a news release said.

The project will cover six blocks between West Magnolia Avenue and Myrtle Avenue, totaling about 2,300 linear feet. Funding will be used to cover construction and operating costs associated with the effort.

The Port of Chickasaw will receive a nearly $7 million federal grant to modernize aging infrastructure after U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) secured a $6,954,000 Port Infrastructure Development Program award for the project.

The funding will rehabilitate docking structures and construct a new bulkhead along both sides of an existing slip at the port — upgrades Britt has pushed for since 2023.

“The Port of Chickasaw is integral to the operations of the Alabama State Port Authority and the Port of Mobile, which is why I have continued working with the City of Chickasaw to get this accomplished over the past several years,” Britt said. “I’m thrilled this grant has been awarded under Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, and I thank him for his leadership in recognizing the importance of this project.”

clean_body: | | | | | | | The U.S. Coast Guard will officially establish its new training center at Birmingham-Southern College later this week, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala., announced Tuesday during a budget hearing with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. Britt, who chairs the Homeland Security appropriations subcommittee, said she will be on the 192-acre campus on Friday with Admiral Kevin Lunday to mark the milestone. | | U.S. Sen. Katie Britt, R-AL, has directly secured $2.063 million for the City of Foley through the Fiscal Year 2026 Homeland Security Appropriations Act to help strengthen the city’s infrastructure and improve storm resiliency during major tropical weather events. The funding, secured by Britt in her role as chair of the Subcommittee on Homeland Security Appropriations, will support a project to relocate vulnerable overhead utilities underground in downtown Foley, a news release said. The project will cover six blocks between West Magnolia Avenue and Myrtle Avenue, totaling about 2,300 linear feet. Funding will be used to cover construction and operating costs associated with the effort. | | - The Port of Chickasaw will receive a nearly $7 million federal grant to modernize aging infrastructure after U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) secured a $6,954,000 Port Infrastructure Development Program award for the project. The funding will rehabilitate docking structures and construct a new bulkhead along both sides of an existing slip at the port — upgrades Britt has pushed for since 2023. “The Port of Chickasaw is integral to the operations of the Alabama State Port Authority and the Port of Mobile, which is why I have continued working with the City of Chickasaw to get this accomplished over the past several years,” Britt said. “I’m thrilled this grant has been awarded under Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, and I thank him for his leadership in recognizing the importance of this project.” | | | | | | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. body:
Washington insiders and the Trump Administration have left behind working Michiganders.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132793240/625697079/680287355?refcode=BLU_EM_MOSS_2026-06-05_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc5OTIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTFiOTJlZjAtMzE2MS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=H4USM4nOPNh7qbPRbYhkqapIfjEfNkTzG_61bjwvMrM=)
---
| Peter,

For the 5th of the month, here are 5 reasons why I’m running for Congress in MI-11:
1. **Defending democracy.** As the Chairman of the Michigan Elections Committee, I stood up for Michiganders’ access to the ballot box in 2020, and I’m not going to stop until every eligible vote is respected.
2. **Lowering costs.** Life has become unaffordable under skyrocketing Trumpflation — I’ll work to cut costs in Washington.
3. **Standing up to Trump.** We need more Democrats in Congress who understand that we can no longer show up to the knife fight with a pie chart. It’s time to actually fight back.

Hey folks,
I sat down with Iowa Democratic Senate nominee **Josh Turek** just days after his primary win, and we got into what's really happening in Iowa right now. We talked about why this race is being overlooked, why voters are hungry for change, and why Josh believes this is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to flip a Senate seat that most people aren't paying enough attention to.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:07**] Josh reflects on his primary victory, winning 96 of 99 counties, and why his message of "prairie populism" connected with voters across Iowa.
* [**00:04:46**] We dig into the economic reality facing Iowa--from healthcare closures to rising cancer rates--and why so many residents feel like their state is moving in the wrong direction.
* [**00:08:01**] Josh lays out his case against Ashley Hinson, arguing that working families are paying the price while corporate interests continue to cash in.
* [**00:10:50**] We discuss culture-war politics, how Republicans are already attacking him, and why he plans to keep the focus on wages, housing, healthcare, and corruption.
* [**00:15:13**] We close with a conversation about why Iowa could surprise people in 2026 and why Democrats shouldn't write off states, counties, or voters that have drifted away from the party.

This episode is about economic frustration, political possibility, and what it looks like when a candidate tries to meet voters where they are instead of talking past them. | |

# [The work is working](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=200479994&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjAwNDc5OTk0LCJpYXQiOjE3ODA3MDA2MjQsImV4cCI6MTc4MzI5MjYyNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.vei7GfB5WgJ4SjMYwMeWT__bBUmYjTl2Y4U0pWSEtaY)
### A new poll confirms what we've been feeling on the ground
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jun 5
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL3RoZS13b3JrLWlzLXdvcmtpbmc_.vbFk75XJaYUSoPdwMmU_CRMuxg0nz9cEcgt79Bxxls8?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/the-work-is-working?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

A new poll came out this week, and it shows we're still leading the field.
That makes at least nine polls now showing us leading.
**And now the RealClearPolitics polling average is showing that I 'm the only Democrat beating Mike Rogers in a head-to-head matchup.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8e40a84d-da86-49be-8366-7d593f979cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I want to tell you what this means.
It means our hard work is breaking through. It means Michiganders are paying attention. It means people are looking closely at this race and asking a simple question: Who can actually beat Mike Rogers in November and get stuff done for Michigan?
Let me say this clearly: Polls aren't perfect. They aren't magic. They do not win races by themselves.
People do. Organizing does. Showing up does.
But polls can tell you whether your message is landing. And what this poll tells me is that Michiganders know this campaign is the real deal. They know I have a deep understanding of the policies that matter to working people. They know I'm a grinder. That I'm relentless. That I'm about the work.
Michigan does not need a senator who is trying to go viral. Michigan needs a senator who delivers for our state.
That's been my whole career.
I helped save 200,000 Michigan auto jobs as Chief of Staff during President Obama's auto rescue. I helped write and pass the CHIPS and Science Act to bring semiconductor manufacturing back to America and to Michigan.
**I was named the most effective Michigan Democrat in Congress. Not because I chase social media likes - it's because I show up, I do the work, and I deliver.**
That's the kind of campaign we are building. Rooted in hard work and grit - the Michigan way. That means tons of conversations with voters. Long days on the trail. Organizing in every corner of this state, including the places too many candidates skip.
And I have to say, I'm loving every minute of it. Michiganders are my people, and this campaign is my love letter.
So this latest poll is encouraging. It tells me we are breaking through.
It tells me something else, too: Republicans know it.
That is why Mike Rogers and his MAGA megadonors have committed tens of millions of dollars to try to turn Michigan red - because the numbers keep showing what they don't want to hear:**I will beat Mike Rogers in November.**
And after I do, I'm going to go to the Senate and fight for Michigan families.
Fight to lower costs.
Fight for manufacturing.
Fight for health care.
Fight for clean water.
Fight for jobs you can raise a family on.
Fight to stop Donald Trump's chaos and abuses of power.
[That's why I'm in this.](https://substack.com/redirect/8e40a84d-da86-49be-8366-7d593f979cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The primary is closer every day. This is the stretch where campaigns either ramp up or they lose steam and get left behind.
For us? We're ramping up. Because if this poll tells us anything, it's that the path is there. We just have to keep pushing. Keep grinding. Keep showing up.
Let's do this. Together.
More soon.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/8e40a84d-da86-49be-8366-7d593f979cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOE MALES FOR CA
body:
I'm humbly asking you to read this, so you can understand why I care so much about this race
| [ ](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=8bb4e0f21eab47afbebf1de91abb6f7d&_e=SKG-RHA_c6QD8uR2vgEq3eB-cYyzRfeGWTcFVjQP7cnHoOwj4IBykGdHSo-7uMx0VKSqtPKsd-wshcVFZAC2bdRl0sdDPsGVI3TewpTfFWUE0czDSbWRMogmC-U2xZdHw8xhIITFqh98F4W6vBKb51hDdsr9dzrIy6mq_n1FgIr_QIQ9CgO4-X0TnVOHPRmfOZE-ItTpzFsiNZSxRDPPdc-SvoUgo94mBf2oiiKCwG5Z3d24fzz6G82jmddfafk_3VQvYgXPwz72sDI7q6DYrf4KRBq2s_EMcU0kaEK6aFhrWAqCSO7VdfsxHHWSb1bDw-oCQcbX1n2a2P3kNo0at2anwHnN54Y1LI3BPvKMDNWw6xqaOSsi0FBoOjuQo5UzOfoJxCImdGo2mcgpMUPBuVVuVzq0yMXYrPCt5mT-ijFndYwIdIXZJCEhd71T5YjFvb32TCZipTELJMyJKTHHxYc7tPq6ni25N8tZoCZT6e3UUEr9ZaDP_I7cMyxtbnFi1DY30tZmH9ocoKqA7wLUXMTsad7a848CQl5_JChXA3Q%3D)
---
Peter,

**My son, who was a U.S. Marine and father of two, was murdered in 2016 when he was just 28 years old.**

[**This is a longer email, but I humbly ask you to read it and consider joining my team at the end.**](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=8bb4e0f21eab47afbebf1de91abb6f7d&_e=SKG-RHA_c6QD8uR2vgEq3eB-cYyzRfeGWTcFVjQP7cnHoOwj4IBykGdHSo-7uMx0VKSqtPKsd-wshcVFZAC2bdRl0sdDPsGVI3TewpTfFWUE0czDSbWRMogmC-U2xZdHw8xhIITFqh98F4W6vBKb51hDdsr9dzrIy6mq_n1FgIr_QIQ9CgO4-X0TnVOHPRmfgTqhJ1cA6lLIc044yz4Xe9Sbe5KYQsHBfO_aKI1-q7tdhB9mB-1VVciv0LRTgNTdPqXoO4GunrZHy6V8Wt_woEbAPcNqe1-3ou24EfIzsRrJMiMa5CS6We6Gpnv6FQ1iNSgsT1MAioSBGQHPJDTdlGxc0PDIfGgKPHHp6kPUFTVWkmy0_pxgYe09xagCiahG9tqd88mYWF2-B7W0Yb0kKfdup1g1gKSDnFTG-_fM8YibdfkzcXCHuhvVIljJo0MosEpogiwD2p6KfFr9HAbGHDFJuCJroEH1gSYS34_CO6VRLrEmwtzrYvg3o5E_2LMYIltQ9kvGPPGwZltUW5-7hasTiIEGav30QAvESCtgHKg%3D)

**In case you don 't know me, my name is Joe Males, and I'm a proud Mexican-American, U.S. Marine Veteran, small business owner, and a city councilman who's running for Congress in CA-25. But above all else, I'm a father who is still in mourning.**

[](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=8bb4e0f21eab47afbebf1de91abb6f7d&_e=SKG-RHA_c6QD8uR2vgEq3eB-cYyzRfeGWTcFVjQP7cnHoOwj4IBykGdHSo-7uMx0VKSqtPKsd-wshcVFZAC2bdRl0sdDPsGVI3TewpTfFWUE0czDSbWRMogmC-U2xZdHw8xhIITFqh98F4W6vBKb51hDdsr9dzrIy6mq_n1FgIr_QIQ9CgO4-X0TnVOHPRmfLX4ehFUby7tqy91SY0d1vB1AVQX37-Xu0pK9P7Dh9wnVXfFikSF6CqiwiUmzGlY1TWRYSZP1A3LtM_P5rJIQGnXcl6IU374lsN3Fo3oZ2yIJ1UGlHvwZU88mpjNX88Ro_q1kvVEoBumQlDbYtP6HUxPOUZI5Xr5D97oySrzzuNVeR6jreB6CpzK4qXkt32IkDBgcQgZvaetf6vPU9z6LZuEurbNEqM45cic1ycYmJPje5HTks309V3OFaBxoq4cyOxG5oxFFZL7Q1AYgeCZW_fdXsQMd4ZcOxyvyAqRnDGap18r2StgSv1bX63Pob3hoy7YN8HFkB3LhSZ2lTLiYgLICtZNBeWOjLAqARbHuRwA%3D)
**I ran for city council and am running for Congress because of my son, Nicholas.**

In 2016, Nicholas came home to visit for his sister's birthday and Father's Day. It was supposed to be a wonderful time to bring our family back together. Then, he was tragically stabbed to death in my hometown of Hemet, California.

[](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=8bb4e0f21eab47afbebf1de91abb6f7d&_e=SKG-RHA_c6QD8uR2vgEq3eB-cYyzRfeGWTcFVjQP7cnHoOwj4IBykGdHSo-7uMx0VKSqtPKsd-wshcVFZAC2bdRl0sdDPsGVI3TewpTfFWUE0czDSbWRMogmC-U2xZdHw8xhIITFqh98F4W6vBKb51hDdsr9dzrIy6mq_n1FgIr_QIQ9CgO4-X0TnVOHPRmfjAi7-qrtNKW8SldammJTsBIEb2Js7UbrVywDD88WHIltIaLp_HkDDdzL0m_en7zHLOwylx9tZsXgwisa8knYfA8MR8OA8DEKcUeSTYaX-owvbBKcNw1Ma8HGYKVRIPq3-nUsqlHks3e8594rLRBGwZaCkN8PIwRT8pHXkSPJna8QO6Gn171uV2IeQOTCpDq6pWldXKPWMRiPFsboIT3xsfIdhH672KgBMJ5jH5SeRTrXuiQvFprVVbbvBvTto9QQYGjMEGUOxecSeB74viAPTmb_19vBFDfRKOFWPVe301MPMWzhHEmmoWYNGpwm0iBah6zuBAg1fcdyfpKrVcPiwdvS7TMqTHMkE-ml7AOLRRE%3D)
No one stepped forward with information on my son's killer, so the case went cold. After five years of not knowing anything about what happened, I decided to do something about it. I ran for City Council, and just a few months later, by the grace of God, they found the killer.

As a parent, losing your child is the most difficult thing to go through. But I'm pushing through it and am committed to making him proud as I fight for a better tomorrow for his children.

I'm grateful to Hemet's law enforcement, who was able to find the killer and arrest him.

Nicholas serves as a daily reminder to me to never take a single precious moment for granted and that I must continue to fight every single day for a better future.

At 4 o'clock this morning, Senate Republicans gave the green light for the IRS to drop ALL investigations into Trump and his family. That’s right, 4 a.m. Almost like they were hoping no one would notice. **Make no mistake: We noticed.** Here's how it went down: Trump's own acting attorney general ordered the IRS to drop every investigation into Trump, his family, their businesses, and their affiliates — including audits that could have cost him more than $100 million. Gone. In exchange, Trump dropped a lawsuit he had filed against the IRS — an agency he controls — that he was using as leverage to cut this deal. Tax experts say this is nothing like a normal IRS settlement. I'll call it what it is: corruption. Democrats brought a bill to the floor to block it. Republicans killed it. If Trump has been evading taxes — and his record strongly suggests that's possible — we will literally never know. The most powerful man in the world just used that power to make sure he never has to pay his taxes. That's not America. That's a monarchy. And it’s a gut punch to every American who works hard and plays by the rules. I won’t stand for it. **I've introduced the Presidential Tax Transparency Act: the President, Vice President, and candidates for those offices must disclose their tax returns for the last 10 years. Posted publicly. And if they refuse, the IRS provides them directly.** No more hiding. No more 4 a.m. sweetheart deals. I'm not going to stop fighting until we get this done. But I need your support. [**If you’re able, will you pitch in $28 or any amount to help stop these kinds of brazen abuses of power? Every donation is another signal that the American people are demanding real change and that no one (not even Trump) is above the law.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3662?amount=28&t=8&akid=2922%2E4032634%2EfEKujw)

I came home tonight, distraught, and decided I had to write down the truth for the one person I trust most: you. Our Majority, and more importantly, President Trump’s future, is hanging by a thread. A single Senate race will decide if the liberals block every single thing he tries to do. If we lose, he is finished. The stakes are overwhelming. I won't be able to look him in the eye knowing I didn't do absolutely everything to keep every seat. Peter, I am appealing to you now, not as a Senator, but as a conservative who has nowhere left to turn. The only way I can possibly move forward is if you read my confidential note, understand the danger, and take action. Please, please, click the link below now. The time for deliberation is over. We need you to save the Majority. With a heavy heart and unwavering determination, Katie Britt US Senator I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong. Faith. Family. Freedom. The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored. From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul. This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere. Will you stand with me? Paid for by Britt for Alabama, Inc. |

Just days away from the beginning of Pride Month, and my colleagues across the aisle remain hellbent on erasing queer history and silencing queer voices. Whether or not they like it, queer and trans people have always been here and will always be here.
